letters.content: I am very worried and upset about our relationship. It's really hard to have a discussion with you when you constantly overreact to whatever is being said. I feel so alone at times when you treat me with such little respect. Your actions and words seem to continue to reinforce how little you care about me or my feelings. For once it would be nice to think that you actually listened to my opinions or feelings before you became defensive. Maybe you don’t realize the negative affect your behaviors are having on my life or maybe you just don’t care. I am feeling very hurt by you and I need you to know that if you can’t seem to make the right choices to be a good parent then I will have to find my own way in life without your help. I hope there is some part of you that recognizes your problem and seeks a way to change this mess. As your child that’s all I can hope for. Please try to be there for me. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

I hope you’ll reconsider and discuss this with me soon. If you continue to ignore my feelings, I’ll have to make future decisions that only ensure my emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and begin to deal with this issue. We need to sit down and talk soon. Thanks for listening.

I have repeatedly shared with you how upset and hurt I am that you are always overreacting to anything that I say or do. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you change your mind and decide you want to work on this, please let me know real soon.  Thanks for listening.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for always overreacting to situations and making you feel that I’m unapproachable. I can see why you would try to avoid conflict with me. The last thing I ever wanted to do was to hurt you in anyway. There is no excuse for a parent to make their child feel so hurt and upset. I promise to listen to your feelings and try to never hurt you like that again. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this. I don't expect forgiveness, but I am truly sorry. Thanks again for sharing your feelings with me.

It really means a lot that you listened to me and tried to make things better for both of us. Your decision to deal openly with me about this issue has helped me gain trust in our relationship again. I'll be here to support you in any way that I can. Thanks for really listening and trying to improve our relationship.

I need to admit that we have been fighting an awful lot in front of you. I wanted to share this with you because I know that you’ve been really affected by this issue. I really feel bad about the way I have acted and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I am writing to tell you how much I appreciate the effort you've made to not fight in front of me.  I know that you have tried really hard to understand my feelings and made real changes to improve our relationship. I want you to know that it means a lot to me when I see you caring to make things better.  I hope that we’ll continue to always be open and respectful toward one another. Thank you so much for really trying to help me with this problem.

I know that you have taken responsibility and apologized for having your adult fights in front of us. I can tell you are genuinely sorry and I appreciate the effort you’ve made to make things better.  It means a lot to me that you cared enough to try to be supportive. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we try to maintain respect for one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we can protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another.  I forgive you. Thank you so much for caring enough to work on this for me.

I know that you think we are always fighting in front of you, but I don’t agree with what you’re saying.  Even though I don’t feel that I have done anything that I need to feel guilty about, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. We’ve always tried to keep our arguments private and away from you. I know you feel differently about this and I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve our differences. I’m sorry that we’re going through this and I wish there was something else I could do or say to help resolve this. Please let’s talk again to try and work this out. Thanks for listening.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for displaying our adult battles and fights in front of you. The last thing I ever wanted to do was to hurt you in anyway. There is no excuse for a parent to make their child feel so hurt and upset. I promise to listen to your feelings and try to never hurt you like that again. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this. I don't expect forgiveness, but I am truly sorry. Thanks again for sharing your feelings with me.

I have repeatedly shared with you how upset and hurt I am that you did two of you continue to fight in front of me. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this.  I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you change your mind and decide you want to work on this, please let me know real soon.  Thanks for listening.

I have already told you how hurt and upset I am that the two of you continue to fight in front of me. I don’t understand why you haven’t made an attempt to talk to me about this.  I’m really disappointed that you don’t think it’s important enough to talk to me. You should really think about the impact this is having on our relationship. I hope you’ll reconsider and discuss this with me soon. If you continue to ignore my feelings, I’ll have to make future decisions that only ensure my emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and begin to deal with this issue. We need to sit down and talk soon. Thanks for listening.

I’m begging you to take your fighting and childlike temper tantrums to a more private area where I am not able to hear them. There is no excuse or reason that you can come up with that justifies arguing and fighting in front of your children. You need to know that this is really hurtful and if you really love me you will try harder to eliminate your fighting in front of me. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

letters.content: It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility and handle your stroke symptoms responsibly. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We certainly aren't always going to agree with one another but I hope we can put this behind us and learn to respect each other’s concerns even when we don't agree. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I ‘m happy to see the effort you are putting into getting well and I completely forgive you for what happened. Thanks for understanding my concern and doing something about it.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your stroke symptoms more responsibly. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make choices that will result in better health. Please call me if you need anything.

I want to share some important personal information with you. I know I can trust you and I feel safe talking to you about this. I wanted you to know that I’m currently going through some medical problems. I’ve been diagnosed with having had a stroke. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I know that I could really use some support and direction from you now. I hope we get a chance to talk soon. Thanks so much for listening.

I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into responsibly deal with your stroke symptoms. Even though it's really difficult to go through any medical problem, you showed you can get through a lot with a positive attitude and a strong desire to remain healthy. You’ve been through a lot of trying times during this whole ordeal but it was your inner strength and dedication that got you going in the right direction with your health. You’ve made us all very proud and we hope we can continue to share life with you for all long time. I’m so happy you worked hard to get well!

I know that you think I haven’t taken responsibility to get help for my stroke symptoms but that’s really not the case. If it were true that I have neglected my health, I would certainly take responsibility and do something about it. I want you to know how sorry I am for any stress or hurt that I have caused you. I know we both see this differently and believe me I feel bad that we're going through this. I’m more than willing to sit down and talk to you about this if you think it could help us.  I wish there was something that either of us could say or do to put this all behind us. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

a.) Level I – Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for a medical condition of stroke.

I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for the stroke symptoms I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I promise I'll make it a point to be evaluated by a professional as soon as possible. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know as soon as I have some news about my progress. Thanks for your help.

b.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for a medical condition of stroke.

I know that you are very upset with me for not getting any help for the stroke symptoms I had. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make when I finally face my problems. It’s easier to think things will just improve on its’ own rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to feel responsible for me just because I refused to seek treatment. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of hurting you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise I’ll do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight the problem head-on and stop fighting with those that love me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

c.) Level I - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for a medical condition of stroke.

I know that you are upset with me for not following through with the treatment recommendations to manage the stroke symptoms I’ve been diagnosed with. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don't know if I'm worrying that the treatment will bring negative side effects, or I’m worrying that I’ll have to make certain changes in my lifestyle that I'm not prepared to make. I realize now that there isn’t any good reason to not follow the recommendations that were given to me. I promise I’ll make it a point to do so immediately. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know how I’m doing as soon as I begin to follow the treatment plan. Thanks for your help

d.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for a medical condition of stroke.

I know that you are very upset with me for refusing to follow through with the treatment recommendations that were given to me for the stroke symptoms I’ve had. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I guess I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make to face my problems and follow the recommendations. It’s easier to think things will just improve on its’ own rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to feel responsible for me just because I refused to seek treatment. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of hurting you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise I’ll do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight the problem head-on and stop fighting with those that love me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

I want to let you know how much I care about you. I’m worried that you’re not seeking help for your stroke symptoms. The problems you are having seem to be worsening and it appears that you have chosen to do nothing to improve your situation or reach out for help. You need to know that all of us who love you and care about you are feeling a need to protect you. If you don’t care about your own health, I realize that I can’t make you care. I just need to make sure that I don’t do anything to reinforce or enable you to continue to disregard your health needs. Because you’re unwilling to seek help, I have no choice but to intervene on your behalf and call your doctor to make him aware of your condition. I refuse to just sit back and watch you go downhill. I want to make sure that I did everything possible to help. This is the only thing I can do to show you how much I love you. It will be difficult on all of us to have to set limits with you, but it may be the only way to get you to realize how important it is to see a doctor. I hope that you will change your mind and seek help to address these health issues. Please don’t let us down. Love,

a.) Level I - Addressing stroke medical condition and lack of follow-through with treatment recommendations for the first time.

I am very concerned that you are not following recommendations to properly care for yourself since you had a stroke. Please don’t let this go. Your symptoms could worsen if you don’t follow those recommendations and I don’t want to see that happen. I care about you and want to see you enjoy life for a long time. So please take the advice your health professional gave you and do what’s best. I will always be here for you, even if you just want someone to talk to. Thanks for listening and I hope you’ll begin to take care of yourself better.

b.) Level II - Addressing stroke medical condition and lack of follow-through with treatment recommendations for the second time.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you actively go against your healthcare professionals’ recommendation. You know what you are supposed to do to care of yourself after a stroke yet you haven’t followed through responsibly. By not taking care of your health, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone who loves you and cares about you. You need to do the right thing and follow your doctors’ recommendation. I am not going to watch you get sicker just because you want to be stubborn. If you continue to refuse medical help, I will figure out a way to ensure you receive proper care. Please do this for me, if not for yourself. I am very concerned and I am here to support you fully. Do us all a favor and just follow the recommendations you were given. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III – Addressing stroke health issue and lack of follow through with treatment recommendations for the third and final time.

I am very upset that you are still refusing to follow the treatment recommendations that were made to help you manage your stroke symptoms. I have offered to help you repeatedly, but you still haven’t followed through with any treatment plan to improve your situation. It’s very difficult to deal with your refusal to care for yourself.  I know I can’t make you take care of your problem, but I can involve health care agencies that will ensure you receive the proper care.  I will always love you and care about you, but I won’t ruin my own health in the process. If you plan to take any steps to seek medical help for this problem, you’ll need to let me know soon; otherwise I will be taking steps to ensure you receive the proper care. I will be waiting to hear from you. Love,

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you ignore serious stroke symptoms that need immediate attention. I am pleading with you to see a healthcare professional to evaluate your medical condition. By not taking care of your health, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone that truly cares about you. You need to do the right thing and follow your doctors’ recommendation. It is too difficult to watch this go on any longer. If you continue to refuse to seek help, I will have to figure out a way to ensure that you are seen by a doctor. Please do this for me, if not for yourself. I am very concerned and just want to help you take the first step. I hope you’ll get in contact with me as soon as possible so we can talk about a plan together. Thanks for listening.

I’m writing to tell you how concerned I am about your health and the stroke symptoms you’ve been experiencing. I really hope that you’ll make an appointment right away to see a doctor about your health concerns. Even though you may find out that it wasn’t serious, it’s better to make sure. And if there is something wrong, you’ll be able to take care of it before it worsens. Please take my advice and schedule a meeting with your doctor or health care professional as soon as possible. letters.content: I want to share some important personal information with you. I know I can trust you and I feel safe talking to you about this. I wanted you to know that I’m currently going through some mental health problems. I have been socially isolating myself from people. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue.  I know that I could really use some support and direction from you now. I hope we get a chance to talk soon. Thanks so much for listening.

I feel that you seem to be isolating from people more often and don’t ever feel like you want to socialize. I’m worried about how this is affecting your life. I really hope you will seek out a doctor or mental health professional to give you some support with this problem. You’ll feel better knowing that you did the right thing to talk to someone knowledgeable about this issue.  I hope you’ll take my advice and go see someone before this gets any worse. I am sure you will feel relieved once you do. I will always be here to give you support if you need me. Take care and thanks for listening.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you ignore the serious problem you’re having with social isolation. I am pleading with you to find a doctor or mental health counselor to evaluate your problem. By not taking care of your problems, you not only hurt yourself, but you’re also hurting everyone that truly cares about you. I promise I will always support you but you really need to talk to someone who can help you. You can’t let this go on without doing something. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III – Addressing Mental Health Issue of Social Isolation.

I am very concerned that your emotional problems are really affecting your ability to enjoy life. I feel helpless as I watch you become more socially isolated. You need to be more responsible to find the right treatment and follow through. I realize that only you can make that happen. I just need to make sure that I don’t reinforce, accept, or enable you to disregard your health. I feel that I need to set stronger limits in our relationship if you refuse to participate in your own care. I will always love you and care about you, but I can’t accept your refusal to get help by turning my head and acting as if nothing is wrong.  I will be there to help you as soon as I know you’ve worked with a professional to develop a treatment plan and are willing to follow through. It is out of unconditional love and utter desperation that I need to do this. I love you very much, but your decision to let this get worse has really hurt me. I hope you will talk to me about this as soon as possible. Otherwise I plan to be setting new limits in our relationship very quickly. I love you and hope you will talk to me. Love,

a.) Level I - Addressing concern about not following through with treatment recommendations for Social Isolation.

I am very concerned that you are not following the treatment recommendations that were given to you by your mental health provider. Your desire to continue to socially isolate yourself from people could easily worsen if you don’t take an active role in your care; and nobody wants to see that happen. I care about you and want to see you get the most out of your life. So please take my advice and follow-through with the treatment plan that was developed for you. I will be here to talk if you ever need me. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II - Addressing concern for the second time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Social Isolation.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you actively go against your doctor or mental health providers’ treatment recommendations. You know what you need to do to treat your social isolation problem; but, you’ve decided not to follow through with what was recommended. By not taking care of your problems, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone that loves you and cares about you. I promise I will be there for you in any way that you need me, as long as you start to take care of your health. It’s impossible for me to be supportive when you are not following the recommendations that could help you. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III - Addressing concern for the third time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Social Isolation.

I am very upset that you continue to not follow the recommendations to treat your social isolation problem. You haven’t followed through with any plan to improve your situation. I don’t understand why you haven’t taken any responsibility to care for your health.  I know I can’t make you take care of your problem, but it still upsets me that you’ve chosen to do nothing to help yourself. I have tried to help you, but at this point, all I can do is set limits in our relationship. I will always love you and care about you, but I won’t ruin my own health in the process. If you plan to follow your health providers’ recommendations, you need to let me know soon. The last thing I want to do is limit our relationship in any way. I will be waiting to hear from you. Love,

a.) Level I – Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Social Isolation.

I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for my social isolation problem. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I promise I’ll make it a point to be evaluated by a mental health professional as soon as I can. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know as soon as I have some news about my progress. Thanks for your help.

b.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Social Isolation.

The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t been responsible to handle my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise that I will do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight rather than hurt the people that mean the most to me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

letters.content: I want to tell you how proud I am for the effort you’ve put into dealing with your mental health problems. Even though it’s difficult to go through emotional problems, you showed you can get through a lot with a positive attitude and a daily commitment to follow through with your treatment recommendations. You’ve been through a lot of trying times recently but you’re commitment to get well has paid off for you. I hope you’ll continue to experience the benefits of all your hard work with a healthy and peaceful life. I am so proud of you!

I want to share some important personal information with you. I know I can trust you and I feel safe talking to you about this. I wanted you to know that I’m going through some mental health problems that have really affected my life. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I didn’t feel I could talk about it until now.  I know that I could really use some support now. It was important for me to contact you to let you know. Thanks so much for listening. I hope we will get a chance to talk soon. Thanks for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your mental health problems more responsibly. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make choices that will result in better health. Please call me if you need anything.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility and handle your mental health problems. I recognize you are sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We certainly aren't always going to agree with one another but I hope we can put this behind us and learn to respect each other’s concerns even when we don't agree. We should always try to protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I ‘m happy to see the effort you are putting into getting well and I completely forgive you for what happened. Thanks for understanding my concern and doing something about it.

I know that you think I haven’t taken responsibility to get help for my mental health problem but that’s really not the case. If it were true that I have neglected my health, I would certainly take responsibility and do something about it. I want you to know how sorry I am for any stress or hurt that I have caused you. I know we both see this differently and I feel bad that we're going through this. I’m more than willing to sit down and talk to you about this if you think it may help. I wish there was something that either one of us could say that would put this all behind us. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

a.) Level I – Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for a General Mental Health Issue.

I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for my mental health problems. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I promise I'll make it a point to be evaluated by a mental health professional as soon as I can. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I'll let you know as soon as I have some news about my progress. Thanks for your help.

b.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for a General Mental Health Issue.

I know that you are very upset with me for not getting any help for my mental health problem. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I have been afraid of all the possible outcomes when I finally face my emotional problems. It’s easier to pretend things will just improve than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I won’t seek some type of treatment. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing all of you than taking action and following through. I promise I’ll do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight the problem head-on and stop fighting those that love me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you as soon as I find out what the experts want me to do. Thanks again.

c.) Level I - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for a General Mental Health Issue.

I know that you are upset with me for not following through with the mental health treatment recommendations that were given to me. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don't know if I'm worrying that the treatment might bring negative side effects, or I’m worrying that I’ll have to make certain changes in my lifestyle that I'm not prepared to make. There's no reason that I shouldn't start following the treatment recommendations that were given to me. I promise I’ll make it a point to do so immediately. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know how I’m doing as soon as I begin to follow the treatment plan. Thanks for your help

d.) Level II - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for a General Mental Health Issue.

I know that you are very upset with me for refusing to follow through with the mental health treatment recommendations that were given to me. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I guess I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make to face my problems and follow the recommendations. It's easier to believe that things will just improve rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t addressed my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing all of you than following through with treatment. I promise I’ll do whatever the treatment mental health professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight and I don’t want to continue to hurt the people that mean the most to me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

I can’t stand by any more and watch you stubbornly ignore the serious emotional problems you’re having. I am pleading with you to contact a doctor or mental health counselor to help you evaluate your problem. By not getting the help you need, you not only hurt yourself, but you’re also hurting everyone that truly cares about you. I promise I will always support you but you really need to talk to someone who can help you. You can’t let this go on any longer without doing something about it. You really need to think about how this is affecting your life and all the people that care about you. We are all very worried and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. I hope we will be able to talk real soon. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III – Addressing General Mental Health Issue.

I am very concerned that your emotional problems are really affecting your ability to enjoy life. I have felt helpless watching your situation worsen. You need to get the proper advice and make a commitment to actively participate in your care. I realize that only you can make that happen. I just need to make sure I don’t reinforce or enable you in some way to disregard your health. By you choosing to not actively participate in your own health care, you have forced me to set stronger limits in our relationship. I will always love you and care about you, but I can’t continue to turn my head and acting as if nothing is wrong. I can’t go on making life easy for you when you’re not taking the necessary steps to ensure your own emotional health and well-being. I won’t be able to help you out in the same way that I have in the past. If you choose to find a health care professional and develop a treatment plan, then I will be there to help you in any way that I can. It’s because of my unconditional love and sense of utter desperation that I need to take this step in our relationship. It may be the last chance I have to let you know how much I love you and how much your decision to not get help for your problem has devastated me. I hope you will talk to me about this as soon as possible. Otherwise I plan to be setting new limits in our relationship very quickly. I love you and hope you will do what’s right for you. Love,

a.) Level I - Addressing concern about not following through with treatment recommendations for a General Mental Health Issue.

I am very concerned that you haven’t followed the treatment recommendations that were given to you by your mental health provider. Your problems could easily worsen if you don’t take an active role in your care and nobody wants to see that happen. I care about you and want to see you get the most out of your life. Please take the advice and be responsible to follow-through with your doctors’ or mental health professionals’ advice. I will always be here for you, even if you just need someone to talk to. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II - Addressing concern for the second time about not following through with treatment recommendations for a General Mental Health Issue.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you actively go against your doctor or mental health providers’ treatment recommendations. You know what you need to do to manage your problems; however, you haven’t chosen to do this responsibly. By not taking care of your problems, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone that loves you and cares about you. I promise I will be there for you, as long as you start to take care of your health. It’s difficult to watch you suffer because of your own fear or stubbornness to reach out for help. You really need to think about how this is affecting your life and everyone who cares about you. We are all very worried and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Please let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III - Addressing concern for the third time about not following through with treatment recommendations for a General Mental Health Issue.

I am very upset that you continue to refuse to follow through with the recommendations that were given to you to help you manage your mental health problem. I have offered to help you repeatedly; however, you haven’t agreed to follow through with any treatment plan to improve your situation. It is very difficult to watch your health worsen as it has.  I know I can’t control your decisions, but it still hurts me very deeply. I am so upset that you have chosen to do nothing about this. At this point, the only thing I can do is set limits with you about our relationship. I will always love you and care about you, but I won’t ruin my own health in the process. If you plan to follow your health providers’ recommendations, you need to let me know soon. The last thing I ever wanted to do is limit our relationship in some way; but your refusal to follow the treatment recommendations has made that a possibility. I hope we will be able to talk about this soon. I will be waiting to hear from you. Love,

letters.content: More and more, you seem to be very negative in your thinking and have been focusing on your failures rather than planning future successes. You really do need to understand that positive thinking is the superhighway to success and happiness. Negative obsessions only lead to furthering your depression and making it more difficult for you to see a light at the end of the tunnel. It's important that you think about all the things that you truly appreciate and have gratitude for in your life. That kind of thinking will help you build a positive sense of well-being. It should be a large part of your daily routine. By believing in the power of hope and by rehearsing positive statements that you know are true throughout your day, you will create a reality that will motivate you to go forward with a more positive outlook and inner confidence. If after several weeks and months of trying to be more positive in your thoughts, you find you are still feeling buried under with negative thoughts, then I will support you in seeking whatever professional help there is to improve your depressive feelings. I love you and care about you. I want to do anything I can to help you feel better. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

We certainly aren't always going to agree with one another but I hope we can put this behind us and learn to respect each other’s concerns even when we don't agree. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I ‘m happy to see the effort you are putting into getting well and I completely forgive you for what happened. Thanks for understanding my concern and doing something about it.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your bipolar symptoms more responsibly. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make choices that will result in a healthier future. You should be proud of the effort you are putting into getting this problem under control. Please call me if you need anything.

I want to share some important personal information with you. I know I can trust you and I feel safe talking to you about this. I wanted you to know that I’m currently going through some mental health problems. I have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue.  I know that I could really use some support and direction from you now. I hope we get a chance to talk soon. Thanks so much for listening.

I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into managing your bipolar disorder. Even though it’s difficult to go through emotional problems, you showed you can get through a lot with a positive attitude and a daily commitment to follow through with your treatment recommendations. You’ve been through a lot of trying times recently but you’re commitment to get well has paid off for you. I hope you’ll continue to experience the benefits of all your hard work with a healthy and peaceful life. I am so proud of you!

I know that you think I haven’t taken responsibility to get help for my bipolar disorder but that’s really not the case. If I felt there was any truth to your concerns I would admit you were right and do something about it. I would still like to apologize for any hurt I may have ever caused you. I know we see this differently and I feel bad that we’re going through this. I’m more than willing to sit down and talk to you about this if you think it may help. I wish there was something that either one of us could say that would put this all behind us. I hope we can sit down and try to work things out. Thanks for listening.

a.) Level I – Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Bipolar Disorder.

I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for the bipolar symptoms I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I promise I’ll make it a point to be evaluated by a mental health professional as soon as I can. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know as soon as I have some news about my progress. Thanks for your help.

b.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Bipolar Disorder.

I know that you are very upset with me for not getting any help for my bipolar disorder. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make when I finally face my problems. It’s easier to pretend things will just improve rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t been responsible to handle my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise that I will do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight rather than hurt the people that mean the most to me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

c.) Level I - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for Bipolar Disorder.

I know that you are upset with me for not following the treatment recommendations that were given to me for the bipolar symptoms I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don't know if I'm worrying that the treatment will bring negative side effects, or I’m worrying that I’ll have to make certain changes in my lifestyle that I'm not prepared to make. I realize now that there isn’t any good reason to not follow the recommendations that were given to me. I promise I’ll make it a point to do so immediately. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know how I’m doing as soon as I begin to follow the treatment plan. Thanks for your help

d.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for Bipolar Disorder.

I know that you are very upset with me for not following through with the treatment recommendations that were given to me for my bipolar disorder. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I guess I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make if I face my problems and follow the recommendations. It’s easier to pretend things will just improve rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t been responsible to handle my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise that I will do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight rather than hurt the people that mean the most to me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you ignore the serious bipolar symptoms you are having. I am pleading with you to find a doctor or mental health counselor to evaluate your problem. By not taking care of your problems, you not only hurt yourself, but you’re also hurting everyone that truly cares about you. I promise I will always support you but you really need to talk to someone who can help you. You can’t let this go on without doing something. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III – Addressing Mental Health Issue of Bipolar Disorder.

I am very concerned that your emotional problems are really affecting your ability to enjoy life. I feel helpless watching your bipolar disorder worsens. You need to be more responsible to find the right treatment and follow through. I realize that only you can make that happen. I just need to make sure that I don’t reinforce, accept, or enable you to disregard your health. I feel that I need to set stronger limits in our relationship if you refuse to participate in your own care. I will always love you and care about you, but I can’t accept your refusal to get help by turning my head and acting as if nothing is wrong.  I will be there to help you as soon as I know you’ve worked with a professional to develop a treatment plan and are willing to follow through. It is out of unconditional love and utter desperation that I need to do this. I love you very much, but your decision to let this get worse has really hurt me. I hope you will talk to me about this as soon as possible. Otherwise I plan to be setting new limits in our relationship very quickly. I love you and hope you will talk to me. Love,

a.) Level I - Addressing concern about not following through with treatment recommendations for Bipolar Disorder.

I am very concerned that you are not following the treatment recommendations that were given to you by your mental health provider. Your bipolar symptoms could easily worsen if you don’t take an active role in your care; and nobody wants to see that happen. I care about you and want to see you get the most out of your life. So please take my advice and follow-through with the treatment plan that was developed for you. I will be here to talk if you ever need me. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II - Addressing concern for the second time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Bipolar Disorder.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you actively go against your doctor or mental health providers’ treatment recommendations. You know what you need to do to manage your bipolar disorder; but, you’ve decided not to follow through with what was recommended. By not taking care of your problems, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone that loves you and cares about you. I promise I will be there for you in any way that you need me, as long as you start to take care of your health. It’s impossible for me to be supportive when you are not following the recommendations that could help you. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III - Addressing concern for the third time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Bipolar Disorder.

I am very upset that you continue to not follow the recommendations to treat your bipolar symptoms. You haven’t followed through with any plan to improve your situation. I don’t understand why you haven’t taken any responsibility to care for your health.  I know I can’t make you take care of your problem, but it still upsets me that you’ve chosen to do nothing to help yourself. I have tried to help you, but at this point, all I can do is set limits in our relationship. I will always love you and care about you, but I won’t ruin my own health in the process. If you plan to follow your health providers’ recommendations, you need to let me know soon. The last thing I want to do is limit our relationship in any way. I will be waiting to hear from you. Love,

I am very concerned about your emotional well-being and the bipolar symptoms you are exhibiting. I really hope you will seek out a doctor or mental health professional to give you some support with this problem. You’ll feel better knowing that you did the right thing to talk to someone knowledgeable about this issue.  I hope you’ll take my advice and go see someone before this gets any worse. I am sure you will feel relieved once you do. I will always be here to give you support if you need me. Take care and thanks for listening.

Even though we've gone through some difficult times, I know that you’ve tried really hard to be there for me in this situation. Thank you so much for the effort you’re putting into resolving this issue.

I realize that I have been extremely selfish and not supportive of the pain and grief your still feeling from mom's death. I'm embarrassed and humiliated by my insensitivity.  I really feel bad about the way I have handled this situation and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I’m really proud of all your support.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility and apologize for not being supportive of my grief process and acting like mom's death didn't matter to you. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I forgive you and hope we can put this behind us.

I know that you think that I'm acting as if mom's death doesn't matter to me anymore; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying.  Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I know you feel differently about this and it’s really unfortunate that this has come between us. I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us get some understanding about this issue. If you’d like to talk about this, please let me know.

I want you to know how sorry I am for giving you the impression that I'm not grieving or that mom's death doesn't matter to me. I want to take full responsibility for not trying to be supportive of your grief process and I promise to do whatever it takes to make sure I'm there for you. Please call me if you need anything.

If it were true that I have neglected my health, I would certainly take responsibility and do something about it. I want you to know how sorry I am for any stress or hurt that I have caused you. I know we both see this differently and believe me I feel bad that we're going through this. I’m more than willing to sit down and talk to you about this if you think it could help us. I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for the Alzheimer problem I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make when I finally face my problems. It’s easier to think things will just improve on its’ own rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to feel responsible for me just because I refused to seek treatment. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of hurting you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise I’ll do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight the problem head-on and stop fighting with those that love me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. letters.content: I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into managing your serious mood disorder. Even though it’s difficult to go through emotional problems, you showed you can get through a lot with a positive attitude and a daily commitment to follow through with your treatment recommendations. You’ve been through a lot of trying times recently but you’re commitment to get well has paid off for you. I hope you’ll continue to experience the benefits of all your hard work with a healthy and peaceful life. I am so proud of you!

I want to share some important personal information with you. I know I can trust you and I feel safe talking to you about this. I wanted you to know that I’m currently going through some mental health problems. I have been dealing with a serious mood disorder. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue.  I know that I could really use some support and direction from you now. I hope we get a chance to talk soon. Thanks so much for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your serious mood disorder problem more responsibly. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make choices that will result in a healthier future. You should be proud of the effort you are putting into getting this problem under control. Please call me if you need anything.

It means a lot to me that you were finally willing to take action and handle your serious mood disorder problem responsibly. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We certainly aren't always going to agree with one another but I hope we can put this behind us and learn to respect each other’s concerns even when we don't agree. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I ‘m happy to see the effort you are putting into getting well and I completely forgive you for what happened. Thanks for understanding my concern and doing something about it.

I know that you think I haven’t taken responsibility to get help for my serious mood disorder problem but that’s really not the case. If I felt there was any truth to your concerns I would admit you were right and do something about it. I would still like to apologize for any hurt I may have ever caused you. I know we see this differently and I feel bad that we’re going through this. I’m more than willing to sit down and talk to you about this if you think it may help. I wish there was something that either one of us could say that would put this all behind us. I hope we can sit down and try to work things out. Thanks for listening.

a.) Level I – Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Mood Disorder.

I know that you are upset with me for not seeking professional help for the serious mood disorder problem I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don’t know if I’m just hoping that things will improve or that I’m afraid to find out what’s wrong. In either case, I know I have avoided what needs to happen. I promise I’ll make it a point to be evaluated by a mental health professional as soon as I can. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know as soon as I have some news about my progress. Thanks for your help.

b.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not seeking treatment for Mood Disorder.

I know that you are very upset with me for not getting any help for my serious mood disorder problem. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make when I finally face my problems. It’s easier to pretend things will just improve rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t been responsible to handle my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise that I will do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight rather than hurt the people that mean the most to me. I also realize that I don’t want to end up shortening my own life by avoiding the truth about my problem. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

c.) Level I - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for Mood Disorder.

I know that you are upset with me for not following the treatment recommendations that were given to me for the serious mood disorder problem I’m having. I wish I could give you a good reason, but there really isn’t any. I don't know if I'm worrying that the treatment will bring negative side effects, or I’m worrying that I’ll have to make certain changes in my lifestyle that I'm not prepared to make. I realize now that there isn’t any good reason to not follow the recommendations that were given to me. I promise I’ll make it a point to do so immediately. Thank you for caring enough and for giving me your support. I’ll let you know how I’m doing as soon as I begin to follow the treatment plan. Thanks for your help

d.) Level II or III - Taking responsibility for not following treatment recommendations for Mood Disorder.

I know that you are very upset with me for not following through with the treatment recommendations that were given to me for my serious mood disorder problem. I do care about all of you, but it has been difficult to do the right thing. I guess I have been afraid of all the changes I’ll need to make if I face my problems and follow the recommendations. It’s easier to pretend things will just improve rather than face my fears and take action. The last thing I want is for you to disconnect from me just because I haven’t been responsible to handle my problems. I know I have hurt all of you and I don’t want to hurt anyone else - including myself. I know I’m more afraid of losing you than going to talk to someone about my problems. I promise that I will do whatever the treatment professionals tell me to do. I’m ready to fight rather than hurt the people that mean the most to me. Thank you for taking the difficult stance that you did. I’ll never forget just how much you went out of your way for me. I’ll get a hold of you soon and let you know how everything’s going. Thanks again.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you ignore the serious mood disorder you are having. I am pleading with you to find a doctor or mental health counselor to evaluate your problem. By not taking care of your problems, you not only hurt yourself, but you’re also hurting everyone that truly cares about you. I promise I will always support you but you really need to talk to someone who can help you. You can’t let this go on without doing something. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III – Addressing Mental Health Issue of Mood Disorder.

I am very concerned that your emotional problems are really affecting your ability to enjoy life. I feel helpless watching your mood disorder symptoms worsen. You need to be more responsible to find the right treatment and follow through. I realize that only you can make that happen. I just need to make sure that I don’t reinforce, accept, or enable you to disregard your health. I feel that I need to set stronger limits in our relationship if you refuse to participate in your own care. I will always love you and care about you, but I can’t accept your refusal to get help by turning my head and acting as if nothing is wrong.  I will be there to help you as soon as I know you’ve worked with a professional to develop a treatment plan and are willing to follow through. It is out of unconditional love and utter desperation that I need to do this. I love you very much, but your decision to let this get worse has really hurt me. I hope you will talk to me about this as soon as possible. Otherwise I plan to be setting new limits in our relationship very quickly. I love you and hope you will talk to me. Love,

a.) Level I - Addressing concern about not following through with treatment recommendations for Mood Disorder.

I am very concerned that you are not following the treatment recommendations that were given to you by your mental health provider. Your mood disorder could easily worsen if you don’t take an active role in your care; and nobody wants to see that happen. I care about you and want to see you get the most out of your life. So please take my advice and follow-through with the treatment plan that was developed for you. I will be here to talk if you ever need me. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II - Addressing concern for the second time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Mood Disorder.

I can’t stand by any longer and watch you actively go against your doctor or mental health providers’ treatment recommendations. You know what you need to do to manage your mood disorder; but, you’ve decided not to follow through with what was recommended. By not taking care of your problems, you’re not only hurting yourself, but you are directly hurting everyone that loves you and cares about you. I promise I will be there for you in any way that you need me, as long as you start to take care of your health. It’s impossible for me to be supportive when you are not following the recommendations that could help you. We are all very worried about you and just want to see you take the right steps to take care of yourself. Let me know as soon as possible, what you plan on doing. Thanks.

c.) Level III - Addressing concern for the third time about not following through with treatment recommendations for Mood Disorder.

I am very upset that you continue to not follow the recommendations to treat your mood disorder. You haven’t followed through with any plan to improve your situation. I don’t understand why you haven’t taken any responsibility to care for your health.  I know I can’t make you take care of your problem, but it still upsets me that you’ve chosen to do nothing to help yourself. I have tried to help you, but at this point, all I can do is set limits in our relationship. I will always love you and care about you, but I won’t ruin my own health in the process. If you plan to follow your health providers’ recommendations, you need to let me know soon. The last thing I want to do is limit our relationship in any way. I will be waiting to hear from you. Love,

I am very concerned about your emotional well-being and the mood disorder you are going through. I really hope you will seek out a doctor or mental health professional to give you some support with this problem. You’ll feel better knowing that you did the right thing to talk to someone knowledgeable about this issue.  I hope you’ll take my advice and go see someone before this gets any worse. I am sure you will feel relieved once you do. I will always be here to give you support if you need me. Take care and thanks for listening.

letters.content: Thank you for being brave enough to face the reality of your addiction and begin taking steps toward healing. That kind of honesty takes courage. I see your effort, and I appreciate every bit of it — for your sake and for the future of our relationship.

Watching you struggle with addiction is one of the hardest things I’ve ever experienced. It scares me, breaks my heart, and sometimes leaves me feeling helpless. That’s part of why I stayed silent — but I know now that silence doesn’t help either of us heal.

You are more than this addiction. I know the person you are beneath it — and I believe in that person’s strength. If you’re ready to face this, I’ll walk beside you. But we need to leave behind anything that makes staying stuck feel comfortable or safe.

I forgive both of us for the ways we’ve gotten caught in this pattern. It’s been hard, confusing, and painful at times. But I still believe change is possible. I forgive the past so we can both move forward with clearer boundaries and deeper support.

I wasn’t trying to enable anything — I was just scared, or unsure of what to do. I didn’t want to push you away or cause a fight. But I’m starting to see that silence can do more harm than honesty. I want to do better from now on.

I’m sorry for the times I tried to “help” by avoiding the truth or protecting you from the consequences. I see now that those choices may have made things worse. I want to take real responsibility now — and support you in ways that are healthier for both of us.

Since I haven’t heard anything and I keep feeling stuck in a cycle I know isn’t healthy, I have to step back. I can’t keep enabling behavior that’s harmful — to you or to me. I’m choosing to protect my well-being while holding space for real change, if and when you’re ready.

I brought up my concern about enabling behaviors around your addiction, but I haven’t heard anything from you. That silence is painful and worrying. I’m still here, and I still care — but we need to talk about this if anything is going to change.

There are times when it feels like I’ve enabled your addiction instead of helping you face it — and I know that’s not healthy for either of us. I’ve made excuses, looked the other way, or tried to keep things calm instead of confronting what’s really going on. I thought I was protecting you — or protecting us — but I realize now that I was helping keep things hidden. That’s not love; that’s fear. I want to support you in ways that are real and honest, not ways that keep you stuck. We both deserve better than living in a cycle of silence and avoidance. Can we talk openly about this and figure out how to move forward in a way that supports actual recovery and healing?

letters.content: Even though we will never judge you based on your outward appearance, people in the world will be constantly judging you on your appearance and public presentation. Many older adults, who will be interviewing you for jobs, teaching you in high school and college and making decisions about your future, will be constantly rating you on your looks, speech, mannerisms, politeness and general personality. You really have one of three choices – 1. Always act and dress as you want, no matter what you are about to be involved in 2. Always try to please everyone's expectations and dress and be who they need or want you to be, or 3. Be yourself in most cases, but for a real important event in your life try to “dress for success” as it's put and present yourself in a way that the job or event dictates. This will give yourself a better chance to achieve the goals you set. Often young people feel that this is an unnecessary demand of society. And to a certain degree, you are right. It's what's inside that counts. It's a normal reaction in society that if someone looks different or appears unkempt, society will believe that the person doesn’t care and is just an unmotivated individual. Often after the person comes to know you, they are less concerned about what you choose to wear or how you keep your hair, piercings etc.; but that first impression will either open or close a lot of doors for you. Being stubborn to always do it your way may close many doors on good opportunities. So make whatever decision you want on how to present yourself to the outside world. But just remember that no matter what you do, we will always love you and support you. We just thought you needed to know and understand how the real world works out there. It may sound like bad advice to tell you to change your outside appearance just to win over someone that may help your future goals be realized; but remember, you aren’t really changing on the inside. Clothes, hair, or outward behaviors will never change your wonderful heart and the great person that you‘ve become. We will always love you and be proud of you.

I am concerned that you need to set healthier boundaries in the relationships that you form. If you follow a few simple but important rules, you’ll save yourself a lot of heartaches in life. Never allow yourself to be controlled, smothered or used by anyone. Always demand to be treated with respect. Never let anyone treat you unfairly, rudely or disrespectfully without holding them accountable immediately. Regardless of how deeply you care for someone, never let anyone convince you to disconnect from your family, leave your education before completion or be involved in any illegal activities. Never tolerate laziness or irresponsibility with anyone who you want to be in a long-term relationship with. You will give them permission to rely solely on you as the responsible one in the relationship. Make sure you don’t agree to engage in any sexual behaviors that you are not ready for or feel comfortable about; especially if you are just trying to keep the individual from leaving you. If anyone pressures you or threatens to leave you for that reason, then they really didn’t love you to begin with. Don’t ever tolerate anyone with a drug or alcohol problem that is not responsibly trying to seek appropriate treatment and help. It’s best to end it quickly if you find out that someone you’ve started to date has a serious alcohol or drug problem and they’re not already trying to take care of it responsibly. Never do anything against your better judgment or intuition. And most importantly never allow anyone to squelch your creativity or take away your dreams. No one should ever be allowed to stop you from living your life to its fullest potential. If anybody tries to do any of these things to you, feel empowered to walk away confidently. Even though you may feel temporarily sad, you will have just saved yourself enormous heartache and pain. Be unashamed and proud that you are willing to set such healthy boundaries in the relationships you’re in; it’s the only real control you have to protect yourself from those that would manipulate, use and control you. Be smart, set boundaries and live happy.

letters.content: I’m proud of you for listening and being open to this talk. It shows a lot of maturity and heart, and I’m here to keep the conversation going whenever you need.
I’ve seen how painful cyberbullying can be — even adults can feel the sting of online hate. That’s why I want to make sure we’re talking about it and not brushing it aside.
If you ever feel like you’re being bullied or pressured online, please speak up. You deserve to feel safe — and you’re brave enough to take that first step toward protecting yourself or someone else.
I forgive you if you’ve said or done anything online you regret. We all make mistakes — what matters is learning from them and trying to be kinder and more responsible going forward.
I don’t think it’s that big a deal — people say stuff online all the time. I can handle it, and I’d rather not make it more dramatic than it needs to be.

Even if you don’t want to talk yet, I hope you’ll remember that I’m always here. My job is to help you feel safe and supported, even if the conversations are uncomfortable.
I brought up cyberbullying because I care about your emotional well-being. I know it’s not always easy to talk about, but I’m still here and ready to listen when you are.

I want to talk with you seriously about cyberbullying, because it’s something that can really hurt people emotionally and mentally — including you or someone you care about. Whether you’re being targeted or see someone else being treated cruelly online, it’s important to understand how serious this is. What happens behind a screen can affect someone deeply, and sometimes people carry that pain quietly. If you’re ever experiencing anything like that or even unsure about something online, please come to me. You won’t get in trouble — I just want to help protect you and help you protect others. This is something we need to be honest and open about so we can face it together.

If there’s one life message, we want you to know, it's that you are special. No other person on this planet has your exact physical, intellectual and emotional makeup. That makes you unique. We didn't want them to know what was going on because we figured they would get mad at us if we told them how we really felt. Unfortunately teenagers keep a lot of what they feel from their parents. We promised ourselves that when we grew up we would never be unapproachable parents. We thought our kids would tell us everything because they would feel so comfortable around us. Unfortunately, we ended up doing the same thing that our parents did and now you only trust us with safe information. We hope we can change that. We don’t expect you to tell us the things that you do that you know go against our values. But we hope that if you get in trouble or develop a real problem in your life you can share it with us. More importantly, you need to not worry about hurting our feelings if you are doing something that you think we’d be upset about. We need to know how you feel. We are your parents and are supposed to be able to protect you and give you the best advice possible. It is not your job to protect us from hurt. If we do anything that makes you sad, angry, or upset and you choose to not tell us for fear of hurting us, then we've failed you as parents. Please don’t worry about hurting our feelings. We know we make plenty of mistakes. You have a right to tell us how we are hurting you or whether we don’t understand how our behaviors or attitudes are affecting you. Please take a risk, open up and talk to us. We're your parents and want to see you happy, no matter what - even if we have to look at ourselves to do so. We’ll love you forever and always be here for you.

b.) Level II: - I am concerned that you're having a difficult time telling the truth.

I told you how concerned I am that you are having such a difficult time telling us the truth. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to set even stricter limits in your life to make you understand how important this is. I hope you change your mind and sit down with me soon so we can talk about this. I love you and only want the best for you. Thanks for listening.

Hopefully you will look at everything that you have read, talked about or had explained by your friends, teachers, church and family; from all that information you will begin to make your own decisions about life. The important thing is to know that your ideas or feelings will likely change many times throughout your life. As you grow older, you tend to view things differently than you might as a teenager. It’s important to try and remain open all your life to different perspectives and experiences. New information will help shape your beliefs. If you stopped and only believed what you currently believe for the rest of your life, you would likely miss the correct viewpoint. Be open to finding the truth for yourself. Try not to put all your faith into one source. Listen to many people. Even as your parents, we have believed in things that we found out later were totally incorrect. No one has all the answers. Listen to what everyone has to say about a particular issue and then develop your position. Once you believe very strongly in a certain way, don’t let the temptation of money, fame, friendship, power or political gain sway you away from your beliefs or behaviors. Your beliefs may change and evolve, but hopefully never for a shallow, selfish or greedy reason. Stay true to your principles by being an honest individual in all your dealings; for it is the honest person that finds true freedom from guilt and a sense of integrity throughout his or her life. We love you and want only the best for you. Always know we are here for you if you become lost or confused on this wonderful yet sometimes confusing journey of life.
