When you were born, I wanted to be able to give you all the beautiful treasures of life. You had love, a nice home, food to eat and clothes to wear. I made sure you had birthday and holiday gifts that let you know that you were special and loved. As you grew up, I never wanted to make you feel like you owed me anything. In fact my whole thought was to just allow you to have a good childhood with few pressures other than school and some chores now and then. Even though I wanted you to have a wonderful childhood, I wanted to teach you the understanding of money and how hard I worked for my money. I wanted to teach you how tough life can be for those who didn't work hard in school or plan properly for their future. Even though I wanted you to learn these valuable lessons, somewhere they became secondary to all the gifts, shopping, trips and overspending I did to show you that I loved you. In hindsight I should have focused more on teaching you patience and discipline rather than trying to give you everything that would make you happy or make your life easy. And that's my fault not yours. And now I am worried that you think the world owes you. I have wrongly taught you that money, houses, clothes, cars and food will just be there with little if any planning or hard work. I’m very worried that you may be really hurt someday when you suddenly realize that life is not going to be as easy for you as it was when you were at home. That is why we feel it is my obligation to help you before you get hurt. And the first thing I need to do is stop treating you like you are helpless and realize that you can and will get your life in order if I give you the power and space to do so. It will be important that once you have your newfound power you will need to act responsibly. You’ll need to make good decisions regarding school, drugs and alcohol, appropriate spending, working hard in a job, choosing the right friends and becoming financially independent from me. Very soon I will need to have you start paying your own bills for gas, snack food, rent, clothes and other personal life expenses. This doesn't mean I’m not going to ever help you out again; it just means we would be putting the majority of responsibility back on you to become independent. I had to do the same thing when I was your age and I know you’ll be able to do it as well. I love you and want to be there emotionally for you whenever you need me. But from now on you need to put real effort into becoming truly independent. Please let's sit down and agree on a plan so that we can all be on the same page. Love,

letters.content: We love you so much. But sometimes we get concerned that you get down and think poorly of yourself. You are a unique individual with many talents and abilities that no one else possesses. People may put you down or try convincing you that you are not as good as they are; but that’s just not true. Who knows you better than you? You know that you are a good person and that you try hard every day to be nice to everyone. That's why you shouldn’t listen to anyone who tries to put you down. As your parents, we see you as a smart and loving person with many positive qualities that will help you be successful in life. You just need to think more positively of yourself without worrying about what others think. Tell yourself repeatedly that you are special and unique and refuse to believe anyone who tries to make you feel bad about yourself. You need to tune them out and tell yourself that they don’t matter. It only matters that your family and real friends love you and think that you are the greatest. We love you very much. Please try and learn to love yourself and become a more confident person. I'll be here to help you in any way that I can. We’ll love you forever and always be here for you.

letters.content: It may feel like the end of the world. Deep inside you ask yourself, “How can I go on? Being in love with someone when you’re a teenager is one of the greatest feelings you can have; but when it ends it can be one of the worst feelings you’ve ever had in your life as well. You tell yourself that you will never allow yourself to be hurt by anyone again. But later in your life you will allow yourself to trust someone again. Being that you are such a very caring person, you will want to love someone and be loved by someone again. Someday you’ll take the risk and start another relationship. It's all part of the cycle of loving and living. Recognize that it's not you that failed but rather the relationship that didn’t succeed. Unless you have experienced a lot of different people during your dating years, you will never truly know when" the right one” comes along. If you marry the first person you ever dated, you will always wonder if you made the right choice. Take this opportunity to explore all the options that you have available to you. When you look back on how you were really treated in this relationship, make sure you honestly assess what went on. Sometimes when we think we are in love we overlook negative parts of the relationship, avoid admitting problems that existed or think that we will fix them later. The end of the relationship is not only a hard time, but should be a time of reflecting and reestablishing your identity. It is a time to get back to the things you like or want to do without first needing to attend to the relationship. At times it feels unbearable; almost like someone close to you has died. However, remember that with loss comes knowledge and opportunity. Don’t let this hard time keep you from learning from the past so that you can move forward more aware and stronger than you were before. Please talk to us and let us know what you are going through so that we can help you. We love you and we promise we’ll help get you through this. Love,

Ever since you were born, you were special to us. You were born with clean lungs, a curious mind and a love for all that life had to offer. Now that you are a teen, you are probably pulled in many directions and I’m sure the pressures at times are great. You know, we love you more than life itself and want you to experience life to the fullest. We also know that you might experiment with alcohol and drugs because of your curious nature or because of some pressure to “fit in”. What you might not understand is that a great percentage of young people who experiment with illegal substances go into heavier use, become addicted and are unable to stop using. Even though I realize you are smart and can figure out things for yourself, I just need to make sure that you know drugs and alcohol can take away your power to have good judgment, act sensibly and make good decisions. We are so afraid that you, like many others, will unintentionally get caught up in using and not even be aware that it's happening. The problem is that most heavy users don’t see a problem with it. Unfortunately, that is the way drugs and alcohol corrupts your judgment and sense of what's best for you. Getting high or being drunk might feel good, or loosen your inhibitions for a short period of time; but in the long run, the lasting effects on your mind and body can be extremely damaging. Just look around you and observe society. Anyone who has put partying in the forefront of their lives from a very young age is usually not happy with their life. They end up needing to alter their mood in order to cope with the hole that they've dug for themselves. It becomes a vicious cycle. The more important priorities of life such as family, education, career, health and spirituality, are put on a back burner. Please try to realize that if you try drugs and alcohol these hidden dangers exist and they may end up seriously altering your life. I have yet to know anyone who in the beginning of their drug addiction ever thought they had a problem. So just be careful and know that addiction can creep up and take away your life when you least expect it. Please don’t be afraid to talk to me or ask me any questions. We might not agree, but you can rest assured I will never steer you in a dangerous direction, because my love for you is unconditional and forever. Love,

We are aware that your schoolwork has gotten harder over the years and even though it's really tough for you sometimes, you have worked hard under our direction to get it done and pass on to the next grade each year. As your high school years begin, we know you have the potential to become anything you want to be as long as you choose to work hard for it. There will be those that don’t have to work as hard as you and others that will struggle much more than you. From this point forward, you will be the only one that will be able to gauge your own needs. The work is going to get more advanced, the homework more frequent and the need to read long boring books for reports and study for difficult tests will become a daily chore. We're hopeful that you realize how important a good education is for your future. The important thing from this point forward is that you truly understand you are completely on your own with your schoolwork. Once you do, I hope you’ll recognize that all the time and effort you are putting in is for your future happiness. We truly hope you begin to understand how important your grades are from this point forward. Every grade you receive will affect the final average on your high school transcript. letters.content: I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into regaining your self-respect and moving forward after the problems you had. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to deal with this situation. We all need to improve our lives by managing the problems that affect us most. Every improvement we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the love and concern we have for one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really proud of all the changes you made.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. I wanted to tell you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I realize that I have had difficulty moving forward after the mistake I made. I need to think more positively and maintain my self-respect if I'm ever going to be happy again. I really feel bad about how I'm handling this and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to move forward after the problems you had. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make the right choices in life. You should be proud of all the hard work you’ve put into managing this problem and the respect you've earned as a result.

It means a lot to me that you are willing to take responsibility and realize that you were having difficulty moving forward after the problems you had. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I accept you acknowledging your mistake and forgive you for what happened.

I know that you think I haven’t moved forward since the mistake I made; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. It’s really unfortunate that this has come between us.  I hope you’re willing to sit down and continue to try to work this out.

I want you to know how sorry I am for not moving forward in my life after the mistake made. The last thing I want to do is make my life more difficult or upset anyone. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner and I promise I will work on getting past this is difficult part of my life. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I'm concerned you're having a difficult time moving forward after the problems you had. Everyone in life has at one time or another done something that they’re ashamed of. How quickly you recover from the embarrassment depends on a few things. First, it's important that you view it as only one of many mistakes that you will make in this life. If you recognize that we all make mistakes and that it is from mistakes that we learn, then you might let yourself off the hook a little quicker. It’s not healthy to constantly view yourself as a failure or a bad person. Secondly, we want you to know that you can’t worry about public opinion. You did what you did and hopefully you learned from it. And for those friends, family and strangers who don’t want to give you another chance, you need to put them out of your head. Who are they to not allow you to recover from this embarrassment? If you take responsibility for what you did and try to fix it, that's all that anyone can ask of you. Anyone that continues to hold you down has their own problems of letting go. If need be, find new friends or people that will continue to accept you even after you've made a mistake. Above all don’t let anyone hold you back from your own healing. We care about you so much and want only happiness for you. We will always be your greatest supporter even during times when you have messed up. Know that we love you and we will always be there for you. Even though you must take responsibility for this, it's not the end of the world and life will go on. Let today be the first day of happiness for the rest of your life. Please sit down and talk to us about what you're feeling. We want to help you get back on track with your life. Love,

I'm very concerned about your views and values regarding material wealth. Although the television and computer lead you to believe that the goal of life is to accumulate nice homes, nice cars and every technological toy available to man, you need to know that those are not the values we want to instill in you. I really want you to understand the pain of people from around the world who have so much less than you currently have. Growing up I saw kids in school being made fun of because their clothes weren't as new or stylish as the other kids or because they didn't have the coolest or most up-to-date sneakers. It was painful to watch those kids being treated so cruelly. I could never figure out how anyone would ever want to laugh at someone else's poverty or hardship. We knew that no one would ever choose to come to school in ripped or outdated clothes if they had a choice. Children and teenagers don’t choose this. It's all they have. And instead of others ignoring the differences, they chose to make them feel bad about their situation. I want you to know that to feel that way about another person is really wrong. I want you to feel compelled to help them in any way possible. Just by being their friend and not being embarrassed to be seen with them around school could really help them feel that they are just as good as the other kids. I really want you to think about how you treat people who are poor, disabled, have no parents, have had difficult lives, have been abused, or are going through serious emotional or physical problems. You need to understand how each one of us represents a miracle of life and that any of us could have just as easily been born into their situation. People feel better when they're loved and accepted and we need to help them feel that way rather than further victimize them into feelings of shame, embarrassment, or sadness.

Regarding all your material possessions and technological toys, it's okay to have them only if you share them with those less fortunate. It's also okay to have them as long as you don't think that because you have them you are in any way more special than those who don’t have them. You need to understand that you could instantly be faced to live without all the material luxuries of life. If I lost my job, if someone died, if we became ill and couldn't produce income we would immediately be in financial trouble. These things happen every day to good hard working people through no fault of their own.  So rather than put yourself above people who have less, be thankful that your current situation isn't as difficult as theirs and give of yourself to others whenever you can. You don’t have to give material goods of food, clothes and money; you can give of your time to be their friend or help them know you care by treating them the same as you would any friend. Because the reality is, you may someday go through what they are going through now. True human success is measured by how you treat others in this life. Are you someone who hurts people, gossips, or humiliates the less fortunate or do you show love to all people and care for them when they need you? Your final measure of success in this life will not be whether or not you had a BMW in the driveway, but rather how you treated all people you came into contact with; not just the ones it was easy and safe to be around.  I hope you really think about this and try to change before life passes you by and it's too late. I care about you and want you to know our real feelings on this issue. I am not sure if we put any pressure on you to feel that you had to be perfect, or it came from somewhere else, but I am concerned that somehow you have the notion that you will be a failure if your performance or achievement is anything less than perfect. First, you really need to understand that there's no such thing as achieving perfection. We are all human beings and there's not a person on the planet that can claim being perfect. We by our own humanity will always be making mistakes. In fact, it is mainly through our mistakes that we learn important lessons in life. If you do make mistakes, the goal should be not to get down on yourself or feel defeated; rather you should identify what the problem is, see if it's fixable and try not to repeat it in the future. You will never be perfect, so striving for it will only leave you depressed and unfulfilled. Instead, try to realize your inner strengths (like the fact that you are kind, loving, honest, etc.) and feel good about who you really are instead of whom you think you should be. Somehow, you need to get over trying to be perfect. It is such an impossible expectation to be placing on yourself and it devours your self-esteem. Know that we think you are great just as you are and so does everyone that knows you. Please don’t be so tough on yourself and accept life's lessons as natural and necessary. You will only face feelings of disappointment and depression if you continue believing that you need to be perfect. By continuing to think of yourself as a perpetual failure you'll never be able to feel good about all the things that should be celebrated in your life. Although the television and computer lead you to believe that the goal of life is to accumulate nice homes, nice cars and every technological toy available to man, you need to know that those are not the values we want to instill in you. I really want you to understand the pain of people from around the world who have so much less than you currently have. Growing up I saw kids in school being made fun of because their clothes weren't as new or stylish as the other kids or because they didn't have the coolest or most up-to-date sneakers. It was painful to watch those kids being treated so cruelly. I could never figure out how anyone would ever want to laugh at someone else's poverty or hardship. We knew that no one would ever choose to come to school in ripped or outdated clothes if they had a choice. Children and teenagers don’t choose this. It's all they have. And instead of others ignoring the differences, they chose to make them feel bad about their situation. I want you to know that to feel that way about another person is really wrong. I want you to feel compelled to help them in any way possible. Just by being their friend and not being embarrassed to be seen with them around school could really help them feel that they are just as good as the other kids. I really want you to think about how you treat people who are poor, disabled, have no parents, have had difficult lives, have been abused, or are going through serious emotional or physical problems. You need to understand how each one of us represents a miracle of life and that any of us could have just as easily been born into their situation. People feel better when they're loved and accepted and we need to help them feel that way rather than further victimize them into feelings of shame, embarrassment, or sadness.

Regarding all your material possessions and technological toys, it's okay to have them only if you share them with those less fortunate. It's also okay to have them as long as you don't think that because you have them you are in any way more special than those who don’t have them. You need to understand that you could instantly be faced to live without all the material luxuries of life. If I lost my job, if someone died, if we became ill and couldn't produce income we would immediately be in financial trouble. These things happen every day to good hard working people through no fault of their own.  So rather than put yourself above people who have less, be thankful that your current situation isn't as difficult as theirs and give of yourself to others whenever you can. You don’t have to give material goods of food, clothes and money; you can give of your time to be their friend or help them know you care by treating them the same as you would any friend. Because the reality is, you may someday go through what they are going through now. True human success is measured by how you treat others in this life. Are you someone who hurts people, gossips, or humiliates the less fortunate or do you show love to all people and care for them when they need you? Your final measure of success in this life will not be whether or not you had a BMW in the driveway, but rather how you treated all people you came into contact with; not just the ones it was easy and safe to be around.  I hope you really think about this and try to change before life passes you by and it's too late. I care about you and wanted you to know our real feelings on this issue. We love you.

A difficult and important part of life is figuring out who are “real friends” and which people are just there for some personal gain. Some people that we call “friends” never intend to give back equally to the relationship.  A real friend is there for you no matter when, where or why you need them. They tend to listen more than give advice and never would judge you, make you feel bad, or hurt you in any way. Some friends that we think of as close friends prove to be just that. letters.content: There are always good choices and not so good choices to make in life. Sometimes we know what to do at the right time and other times we don’t know until it's too late that we made the wrong decision. There are times when people even know the decision they're about to make is the worst of several options and they choose to do it anyway. Anytime someone does that, it's difficult to understand how they came to that final decision. Maybe they don’t care enough about themselves or possibly they are depressed or have low self-esteem. Maybe they have an “I don’t care attitude” about their life or they had already given up trying to be truly happy or healthy. Sometimes they go along with the crowd just to fit in so that people will accept them or like them. Your choices in life should never be made based on who will like you or accept you. Your choices should be made only after you have considered the impact such decisions will have on your life. You will always need to determine if you are putting yourself or your reputation at risk; and whether others could possibly be hurt by your decision. Will family members be hurt by the decision? How will the decision affect your future opportunities in life? Did you know that being arrested by the police may limit what profession you can work in for the rest of your life? Your choices may ultimately limit your ability to be an elected official, work in a local, state, or federal government job, enlist in the military, be a lawyer, judge, police officer, probation officer or work with kids in any capacity. Your decisions will shape the kind of life you can have. So making those important choices based on whether some friend or group of so-called friends will want you around is selling yourself and possibly your whole future down the river for some momentary acceptance by your friends; attention that may be there today but be gone tomorrow. Be strong and recognize you need to help your own cause rather than be your own worst enemy. If you really don’t care about your life anymore let someone know so that you can get the help you need. You are important and you are loved. And only you can make the final difference in your life - not a friend or even a family member can affect your life as much as the decisions you make. Sky’s the limit in life if you make good decisions throughout it. I will always be here for you if you need me. I love you unconditionally and forever.

letters.content: Graduating from school is never easy though some may think so. It's never quick even though many years from now it may feel it was. Graduation day represents the final curtain call of a grand play where you were the writer, director, sound and light crew as well as all the actors in the production. You performed literally thousands of scenes without a single applause. Today is your day to capture all that applause that was due you. Oh sure, there was encouragement to meet deadlines, learn your lines, build the proper set, participate in a dress rehearsal and take cues from the director. However, after each performance there were few if any standing ovations. Even a few jeers could be heard in the background from time to time. Rarely was there any thunderous appreciation for all your hard work. Well today, we applaud you and come to our feet to say that the performance was magnificent. It was a long time and you never gave up. You showed remarkable effort and patience in delaying immediate gratification. This is a day for rejoicing. We have never been prouder -- oh, except for one other time; the day you were born. Love you and wish you nothing but happiness and success for your future. We’ll love you forever and fully support you in all of your life’s’ endeavors. Congratulations to our graduate.

I know this loss has been really hard time on all of us and I know that in order to grieve properly you need to know that it's natural to cry, feel anger, be confused and even need to have some questions answered. At times, you may feel somewhat numb and not at all like yourself. One thing that's certain, we are all here for you and we need you as much as you need us to help each other get through this. Looking at pictures, talking and reminiscing about the past times together -- even laughing about some of those memories-- will help us ease the pain that we’re all feeling. It's okay to cry together and hold each other when we feel the need. It’s okay to even talk out loud to the person we miss even though they aren’t here physically; we all want to believe they are still with us and talking to them out aloud can be comforting. There may be times where I will need a hug and I don’t want you to feel ashamed to ask me for one. Everything you feel or are going through is normal. Anyone that loses someone they love goes through a lot of the same feelings that you are going through. I guess it's good to know that we’re not going crazy or something when we feel like that. Even though we think this pain will never end I promise you that we will get through it. And if we grieve together as a family there's no doubt our pain will pass even sooner. So let's start by at least sitting down and talking openly about what we are feeling and thinking and hopefully we'll all find some relief in sharing our sadness and pain together. We love you and I promise we will make it through this hard time together. Love,

Baby dolls and pink frills don’t excite you as they once did. Music, style and boys are some of your top priorities now. Not always in that order of course. I want you to understand some things that I wasn't told or at least refused to believe when I was your age. Almost all the boys in their teens are looking for a sexual relationship with their girlfriend. They may start out by claiming that they will wait until you are ready, while staying with you in hopes that you’ll gain stronger feelings for them. Then at some point, and it's different for everyone, they may try and flip your decision into a guilt trip. ”If you truly loved me, you would”. Or “if you won't, there are plenty of girls who will”. Please don’t fall for those lines of deceit and manipulation. If you go along with his demands you will truly regret it. Nine out of ten times, this “love of your life”, will lose interest once he achieves his goal. And you will be left feeling hurt and used. Instead of playing along with his game, have a game of your own. In every dating situation, be very clear to the guy that you have strong values and beliefs about waiting till after marriage to have any type of sexual relations. See how long it takes for his pressuring advances to occur. Continue to be strong and reinforce how you will never change your decision on waiting till marriage. If after nine months to a year you are still dating and the young man is still respecting your wishes, he may be someone with high values himself that deserves your trust. Hopefully you will end up having a great relationship with this individual without being involved with sex; and you will never have to lose your self-respect giving into his sexual advances when you aren’t ready or feel uncomfortable to do so. I love you and only want the best for you and your future. And I trust you’ll make the right choices for yourself. I will always be here for you if you need me. I love you unconditionally and forever.

letters.content: I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into improving your self-esteem and realizing the you are just as good as any of your friends. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to deal with this situation. We all need to improve our lives by managing the problems that affect us most. Every improvement we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the love and concern we have for one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really proud of all the changes you made.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. I wanted to tell you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I realize that I often think that my friends are better than me and I know deep down that I shouldn't be thinking that way. I really feel bad about how I have let myself believe this for so long. I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your low self-esteem and change your view that your friends are better than you. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make the right choices in life. You should be proud of all the hard work you’ve put into managing this problem and the respect you've earned as a result.

It means a lot to me that you are willing to take responsibility and recognize that you are just as good as your friends are. I know that you are sincerely sorry for ever having thought otherwise. I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I accept you acknowledging your mistake and forgive you for what happened.

I know that you think I believe my friends are better than me; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I feel that I am just as good as they are and I recognize my strengths in life. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. It’s really unfortunate that this has come between us.  I hope you’re willing to sit down and continue to try to work this out.

I want you to know how sorry I am for always thinking my friends are better than me. The last thing I want to do is make my life more difficult or upset anyone. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner and I promise I will continue to work on this. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I'm concerned that you think that your friends are better than you most of the time. I'm worried that you're too hard on yourself and that this could lead to a lot of problems down the road. I know that sometimes you feel like you can’t do things as good as other kids; but I want to tell you that we think you do a lot of things better than most kids your age. You are one of the nicest people we know and although you might not see that as a big deal, to us it is the most important thing in life. You are also one of the most caring people we know and although you feel there are activities you may not be as good at as your friends, I don’t know any of your friends to have as big a heart or caring concern for people than you have. Success in human terms is not measured in how high you jump or how fast you run, but how deeply you care and love others. You have begun to show this as one of your strongest points and you should be proudest of this part of your character. We certainly are very proud of you. You may feel less than others at times; however, we know the truth. You are one of the greatest kids any parent could ever have. We’ll love you forever and always be here for you. Always try to be proud of yourself. I hope you'll sit down and talk to us about your feelings. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II: - I'm concerned you think that all your friends are better than you at most things.

I told you how concerned I am that you think all your friends are better than you. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I can only hope that someday you realize the need to deal with this issue. I hope you change your mind and sit down with me soon so we can talk about this. I love you and only want the best for you. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III: - I'm concerned you think that all your friends are better than you at most things.

I have repeatedly shared with you how concerned I am that you think all your friends are better than you. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. I can only hope that someday you realize the need to deal with this issue. If you decide that you want to work this out, you need to let me know real soon. I hope you decide to talk and I can help you with this. Thanks for listening.

It seems that no matter how hard we work, how much we plan, or how careful we are in making important life decisions, there will always be hard times in our life where we feel like a failure or we just want to give up. The most important thing to know is that everyone -- that’s everyone -- goes through periods like that. And what's even more difficult is that sometimes those bad times seem to last forever when you are in the middle of them. The most important thing you need to understand is that bad times are only temporary. They may feel like there is no way out or that they’re going to last forever; but I promise you that the sun will rise again on your life. You have to start by believing and thinking positive thoughts about your difficult situation. Thinking positive can change how you feel about your problem and if you talk about how you feel you will begin to hurt less, feel more strength and realize that you are going to survive it. We love you and know there will be many times as you grow up that you will go through times like that. Please don’t despair and by all means, never give up. For the day, you give up, maybe just hours or even minutes from when the tough times were about to get better. You just never know. I know that you have always been a survivor since you were born. And I know deep inside, you have the inner strength and will to live and find happiness. You just need to know that I am always available to you if you need me. Open your heart and you will find a way through the tough times. Please promise me that you will never seriously consider suicide as it’s merely a permanent solution to a temporary problem. Killing yourself is also a selfish act because you'd be killing all of us at the same time. We would never get over losing you and our life would be ruined forever. I love you more than life itself and couldn't stand being on this earth one day if you took your life. There are always better options and I need to make sure you understand that. I promise that I will always be there to help you even when if it feels like it will be impossible to get through it. I’ll love you unconditionally forever.

a.) Level l –I am worried you don't understand how your outward appearance will be judged by society.

I am worried you don't understand how your outward appearance is constantly being judged by society. Even though we will never judge you based on your outward appearance, people in the world will be constantly judging you on your appearance and public presentation. Many older adults, who will be interviewing you for jobs, teaching you in high school and college and making decisions about your future, will be constantly rating you on your looks, speech, mannerisms, politeness and general personality. You really have one of three choices – 1. Always act and dress as you want, no matter what you are about to be involved in 2. Always try to please everyone's expectations and dress and be who they need or want you to be, or 3. Be yourself in most cases, but for a real important event in your life try to “dress for success” as it's put and present yourself in a way that the job or event dictates. This will give yourself a better chance to achieve the goals you set. Often young people feel that this is an unnecessary demand of society. And to a certain degree, you are right. It's what's inside that counts. It's a normal reaction in society that if someone looks different or appears unkept, society will believe that the person doesn’t care and is just an unmotivated individual. Often after the person comes to know you, they are less concerned about what you choose to wear or how you keep your hair, piercings etc.; but that first impression will either open or close a lot of doors for you. Being stubborn to always do it your way may close many doors on good opportunities. So make whatever decision you want on how to present yourself to the outside world. But just remember that no matter what you do, we will always love you and support you. We just thought you needed to know and understand how the real world works out there. It may sound like bad advice to tell you to change your outside appearance just to win over someone that may help your future goals be realized; but remember, you aren’t really changing on the inside. Clothes, hair, or outward behaviors will never change your wonderful heart and the great person that you‘ve become. We will always love you and be proud of you. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this.  I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t want to help me with this and that I need to seek that information on my own. If you decide to change your mind and want to talk, please let me know soon.

I have already told you that I wanted you to help me find information about my biological parents. Unfortunately, you haven’t made any effort to sit down and discuss the issue.  I’m really disappointed that you won’t talk to me. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon.  If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to seek that information on my own. I hope you change your mind and I hear from you soon. Thanks for listening.

The day you told me I was adopted, you also told me that if I ever wanted information about my biological parents, you would provide that for me. I’m very interested in learning more about them and I need the help that you once promised. Please understand that my desire to want to get to know my biological parents will never change my love and appreciation for all you have done in raising me. I will always love you and consider you my only real parents regardless of what happens in meeting any biological members of my family. I look forward to talking with you about this. Thanks for helping.

You once told me that if I ever wanted more information about my biological parents, you would help to provide me with that. I have been thinking a lot about my adoption and would like to find out more about my biological family. Even though I'm choosing to know more about them, I don't want you to interpret that as a desire on my part to seek them out or meet with them. I just want to get any available information so that I can decide down the road whether I want to try and find them. I really appreciate any help that you can give me and above all I want you to know how much I love you and appreciate you. Thanks in advance for your help.

letters.content: Congratulations on the effort and energy that you put into dealing with your academics more responsibly. It has been a long and difficult road but your dedication has definitely paid off. It was amazing to see the consistent effort and motivation you put into this. I'm extremely proud of you and hope to continue to share in your successes throughout your life. Congratulations on a job well done! Be proud!

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. I wanted to tell you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I realize that I have been slacking off a lot in my academics and I need to be more responsible and take it more serious.  I really feel bad about the way I have handled this situation and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to deal with your academic program more responsibly. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make the right choices in life. You should be proud of all the hard work you’ve put into managing this problem and the respect you've earned as a result.

It means a lot to me that you are willing to take responsibility and apologize for not taking your academics as serious as you should. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I accept you acknowledging your mistake and forgive you for what happened.

I know that you think I'm not taking my academics seriously enough; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. I’m willing to apologize for any mistakes I have made; but I don’t believe I did anything in this situation that I should have to feel bad about. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. It’s really unfortunate that this has come between us.  I hope you’re willing to sit down and continue to try to work this out.

I want you to know how sorry I am for not taking my academics more seriously. The last thing I want to do is make my life more difficult or upset anyone. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner and I promise I will continue to work on this. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

It has been a while since we gave you the responsibility to handle your academics. Unfortunately I haven’t seen any evidence of you putting serious effort into your schooling. I had hoped that you would understand how important your grades were from this point forward. I thought you would try and to receive better grades so that you could be proud of your final average rather than shrink in humiliation when you have to report them to a college admissions board or future employer. Even though I'm not on your back anymore as I once was about your academics, I'm still concerned for your future success. I just want you to know that I'm still here if you need my help. I hope you’ll begin to take a more responsible attitude toward all the demands that are being placed on you in high school. You need to know that I'll always be there for you emotionally no matter what you choose to do with your life. But it hurts to see that you still don't recognize the importance of your education. Please think about what I'm saying the next time you're thinking about making a bad choice with regard to studying, homework, class participation, or any school work. I hope we can sit down and talk about this so that I know that you understand my concerns. I love you.

b.) Level II: - I'm concerned that you haven't become personally responsible for your academics.

I told you how concerned I am that you haven't become personally responsible for your academics. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon and you eventually figure out on your own how important your academics are. I hope you change your mind and sit down with me to talk about this. I love you and only want the best for you. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III: - I'm concerned that you haven't become personally responsible for your academics

I have repeatedly shared with you how concerned I am that you haven't become personally responsible for your academics. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. You’ve left me no other choice but to allow you to suffer the natural consequences of your choices.  If you decide that you want to work this out, you need to let me know real soon. I hope you decide to talk and I can help you with this. Thanks for listening.

topics.name: It’s important that you never feel so desperate about a problem that you don’t want to live.

letters.content:
I know we've talked about adopting many times and it's clear to me that you are absolutely ready to adopt a child; however, I really need you to understand that I am absolutely against adopting. Our relationship may not survive such brutal honesty, but I need you to know that I will never be able to take on such a significant obligation and responsibility at this point in my life. If I did go along with that decision, I would feel anger and resentment for having been forced to do something that I was clearly against. If we are going to remain together, this decision requires both of us to have input and come to some understanding. At this point in my life, I don’t ever see my feelings changing about this issue. If adopting a child is that important to you and you need to follow through, then we are going to have to separate. I hope we can sit down and talk about this as soon as possible. I'm sorry I can't just say yes to show you how much I love you; but, this particular decision affects my life in too many ways to just say yes.  I hope you understand how I feel about this. I’m sorry that I don’t feel the same way about this that you do. Thanks for hearing me out.

After giving it a lot of thought I have decided that I would never be able to adopt a child. Even though I thought at one point that maybe I could, I have realized that it's unrealistic under the circumstances. I'm sorry if this is painful for you to hear; I never meant to hurt you. I just know that I would resent that decision for years if I made it feeling the way I do now. I know I can’t control your decision, but I thought it was time to be 100% honest with you about my feelings. Please let’s sit down and talk about this and come to a final understanding one way or the other. Regardless of that decision, I will always love you and care about you and hope that you find true happiness.

I have already told you how committed I am to never adopting a child. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to make future decisions that will ensure my own emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and I hear from you soon. Thanks for listening.

I have repeatedly shared with you how committed I am to never adopting a child. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this.  I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you decide to change your mind and want to talk, please let me know soon.

a.)Level I - Taking responsibility and apologizing for realizing that I will never be able to adopt a child.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for realizing that I will never be able to support the two of us adopting a child. The last thing I ever wanted to do was to hurt you. I am sorry for the way that I feel and I'm sorry that my decision is upsetting to you. I don’t expect you to forgive me, but I am truly sorry.   I would like us to sit down and talk about our feelings on this. But if you choose not to I will understand. I hope you’ll talk to me soon. Thanks for listening. I

I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into trying to understand my decision to not want to ever adopt a child. It probably was very hard for you to be supportive at first, but I am very thankful that you’ve tried to have an open mind. Every positive change we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the trust that we share with one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really happy that you’ll reconsider adopting.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. It’s hard to admit this, but I realize that I have completely ruled out the possibility of us ever adopting a child. I feel that I haven’t been honest with myself or you about this, but I finally need to be honest with you. I’d like to sit down and talk to you about this soon. Thanks for listening.

I wanted to let you know how much I appreciate your decision to rethink the possibility of us adopting a child. You and I have made it through a lot of difficult times and we’ve learned to support each other even when our relationship is struggling.  I appreciate the effort you’ve put into to thinking about adopting. I know if we continue to support one another our relationship will remain strong. We need to insist on being respectful towards one another and honest.  Thank you so much for trying to understand my feelings and being supportive to at least once again talk about the possibility of adoption.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility and apologize for saying you would never adopt a child with me. I can tell you are genuinely sorry and committed to do whatever it takes to work through this problem. It means a lot to me that you wanted to understand my feelings and be supportive. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another.  I forgive you. Thank you so much for caring enough to work this out with me.

I know that you think I am opposed to adopting a child, but that just isn't true. I don’t believe that I have ever ruled out the possibility of adoption. I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you; but I have never concluded that adoption was out of the question.  I know you feel differently about this and it’s really unfortunate that this has come between us. I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve our differences. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

I'm sure there were a lot of discussions and maybe even some disagreements about that decision. Now that I'm older, all of that information surrounding your decision is important to me. I think it's important that I really understand why you decided to adopt me given that it had such an impact on my life. I hope you can understand why the particulars mean so much to me. I hope you'll sit down and answer the questions that I have. Above all, I want you to know how much I love you and appreciate you. Thanks for adopting me. Love,

Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I am very concerned that you're not making good choices for yourself. There are always good choices and not so good choices to make in life. Sometimes we know what to do at the right time and other times we don’t know until it's too late that we made the wrong decision. There are times when people even know the decision they're about to make is the worst of several options and they choose to do it anyway. Anytime someone does that, it's difficult to understand how they came to that final decision. Maybe they don’t care enough about themselves or possibly they are depressed or have low self-esteem. Maybe they have an “I don’t care attitude” about their life or they had already given up trying to be truly happy or healthy. Sometimes they go along with the crowd just to fit in so that people will accept them or like them. Your choices in life should never be made based on who will like you or accept you. Your choices should be made only after you have considered the impact such decisions will have on your life. You will always need to determine if you are putting yourself or your reputation at risk; and whether others could possibly be hurt by your decision. Will family members be hurt by the decision? How will the decision affect your future opportunities in life? Did you know that being arrested by the police may limit what profession you can work in for the rest of your life? Your choices may ultimately limit your ability to be an elected official, work in a local, state, or federal government job, enlist in the military, be a lawyer, judge, police officer, probation officer or work with kids in any capacity. Your decisions will shape the kind of life you can have. So making those important choices based on whether some friend or group of so-called friends will want you around is selling yourself and possibly your whole future down the river for some momentary acceptance by your friends; attention that may be there today but be gone tomorrow. Be strong and recognize you need to help your own cause rather than be your own worst enemy. If you really don’t care about your life anymore let someone know so that you can get the help you need. You are important and you are loved. And only you can make the final difference in your life - not a friend or even a family member can affect your life as much as the decisions you make. Sky’s the limit in life if you make good decisions throughout it. I will always be here for you if you need me. I love you unconditionally and forever. Please talk to me soon about my concerns. Thanks for listening.

letters.content:
I’ve been really worried that sometimes you feel so desperate you don't want to live. It seems that no matter how hard we work, how much we plan, or how careful we are in making important life decisions, there will always be hard times in our life where we feel like a failure or we just want to give up. The most important thing to know is that everyone -- that’s everyone -- goes through periods like that. And what's even more difficult is that sometimes those bad times seem to last forever when you are in the middle of them. The most important thing you need to understand is that bad times are only temporary. They may feel like there is no way out or that they’re going to last forever; but I promise you that the sun will rise again on your life. You have to start by believing and thinking positive thoughts about your difficult situation. Thinking positive can change how you feel about your problem and if you talk about how you feel you will begin to hurt less, feel more strength and realize that you are going to survive it. We love you and know there will be many times as you grow up that you will go through times like that. Please don’t despair and by all means, never give up. For the day, you give up, maybe just hours or even minutes from when the tough times were about to get better. You just never know. I know that you have always been a survivor since you were born. And I know deep inside, you have the inner strength and will to live and find happiness. You just need to know that I am always available to you if you need me. Open your heart and you will find a way through the tough times. Please promise me that you will never seriously consider suicide as it’s merely a permanent solution to a temporary problem. Killing yourself is also a selfish act because you'd be killing all of us at the same time. We would never get over losing you and our life would be ruined forever. I love you more than life itself and couldn't stand being on this earth one day if you took your life. There are always better options and I need to make sure you understand that. I promise that I will always be there to help you even when if it feels like it will be impossible to get through it. I love unconditionally forever. I hope we can talk soon about this. Thanks for listening.

It certainly wasn't planned when we got married that we would ever be separating and it certainly hasn't been easy going through it. However, we all need to understand what this means so we can adjust to what's happening. The most important thing that you need to know is that you were never in any way responsible for the problems in our relationship. Did we ever get stressed out or frustrated by you? Of course, but that kind of stress or trouble does not make a marriage breakup. That’s just the normal stress of raising a family. There are a million reasons why parents end up separating or divorcing; however, none of them can ever be explained by blaming the children; even if the children were really difficult or had a lot of problems. If anything, problems such as those should bring parents closer because they need to be a team to best support their child who's having the difficulty. So as far as blaming yourself on some level, you need to truly understand that you had absolutely nothing to do with our separation.

The next important thing that is going to help you adjust to this situation is to know that it is okay to show love and respect to both of your parents. You don’t need to form loyalties with either parent. If you do, it should be because it's your choice and not because of feeling guilty or influenced by one of us. It's best if you try to stay out of the middle of our problems. We are big people and can handle our own hurts and troubles. It is not necessary for you to fight our battles or get mad at the parent that may be acting spiteful or revengeful. If either parent acts mad at you directly, that's different and you will need to decide how you want to handle that. You can handle it on your own, ask to talk to one of us or use a third party like a counselor or law guardian to give you some advice. You need to know we want you to love and respect both of us unless you see reasons o your own to do otherwise. You should never judge either parent based on information of one parent talking about the other parent. Form your own judgments throughout your life while visiting, observing and talking to each parent. Hopefully we will behave in ways that will allow you to respect both of us and love us fully. However, that will depend on how we treat you and the amount of support, time, attention and love you receive from us. Unfortunately, because there will be visitation times when certain family members will have to separate from one another,  adjustments will need to be made on all our parts to make the best of a not so ideal situation.

You also need to know that we want to hear your opinions and feelings even if you think it will hurt one of us. If it does upset one of us, it will be our responsibility to handle it. You should not feel guilty about it. You need to know you must try to be open to tell us what you are feeling and thinking. We want to help you through this as best we can. Our job is to care for you and make sure that you are as well adjusted to this separation as possible. So knowing your thoughts and feelings will really help us guide you through this. And as far as who you want to live with, your feelings on this may change several times over the course of your teen years. So just be open with both of us on how you feel. Remember you are not hurting us if you express your true feelings. We would really be hurt if you weren’t honest with us to spare us some pain. So try not to worry about hurting us with your true feelings and please, if we screw up, tell us - we're only human.

Although it’s early to be talking about this, someday we may want to move forward in our lives to start a new adult relationship. Even though we are entitled to do so, we would absolutely want to know your opinions and feelings if a relationship we were in, became more serious. We would want to include your feelings into any decisions we were making. And if we did get involved with someone and it resulted in problems for you, we would want to hear from you so that we could resolve the problem. Your feelings are the most important thing to us.

The final thing that I want you to understand about our separation is that the amount of money that each of us have to raise you may be different at times. Although we will do everything in our power to make this transition as smooth as possible, it would be helpful if you understand we are trying to do the best we can at any particular moment. And if at times there ends up to be less money or if we ever needed to move from one of our homes for some reason, you need not panic. We will still have each other and I promise you that you won't go hungry or be without a home. We will survive any problem that comes up. It may just take some time to get fully back on our feet. None of those types of problems need ever be your concern. Worrying about finances or other adult matters is not something you should ever have to think about. You just need to know that you are loved and you will be taken care of. We will do everything in our power to make this work for you and for us as a family. By all means, if you are scared, talk to us and we will show you that we will both be there for you. Remember you are not at all to blame for what is happening and if we could prevent you from going through this we would.

As much as you are not to blame for this situation, nothing you can say or do will be able to prevent the separation from occurring. You may feel angry, sad, or even helpless knowing that you can’t make things go back to the way they were. Eventually you will see that we are still a family and that you are still loved and cared for as much as you were before. What’s most important is that you always remain open with us and don’t fear hurting either one of our feelings. We need you to tell us what's on your mind. And even though we are going through some harder times now, you have to remember we are your parents and you are our first priority. Your well-being means everything to us. Helping you get through this will help us to heal more quickly as a family. So please don’t hesitate to talk to us openly and honestly. We love you and only want the best for you. We never want you to be put you in the middle of our disagreements or be used as a messenger or a sounding board against the other parent. If that ever happens, you need to let us know immediately. In the end the most important responsibility you have is to make sure you tell us how we're doing. You came into this world as part of our family and we will all get through this together as a family. We love you.

I'm worried you're getting down on yourself for your mental health problem. I know that you are feeling bad about the symptoms that you are having and we wish we could take away that stress in your life. The main thing you must believe is that these symptoms are not any different than having a sore throat from strep, vomiting because of a stomach bug or having fatigue from a heart condition. Instead of being symptoms of your throat, stomach or heart they are symptoms of a different part of your body - your brain. Years ago, we knew very little about the brain. People thought that symptoms such as depression, anxiety, panic attacks, delusions or even hallucinations, were from demons or from some evil source outside the body. How ridiculous that turned out to be. Because science couldn't pinpoint, the source of the symptoms, society made up false reasons for the conditions of the brain. Now we know differently and understand that these symptoms occur just as any other disease does. We now accept that the symptoms originate directly from the neurology and chemistry of the brain. Unfortunately, some of the old thoughts haven’t left society. Some people are still afraid when they see people who have these symptoms. Other people can be cruel and call people names like crazy or insane. Why don’t they make up names for diabetes like sugar wimp or for heart disease like blood pump pansy? Because it makes no sense, that's why. And it's ridiculous that some people are freaked out when they find out their friend or family member has a mental or emotional illness. Society is getting somewhat better and hopefully in the coming decades the public will have enough information for everyone to better understand these issues of the brain more thoroughly. But for now, all you need to know is that there is no difference between illnesses of the brain and illnesses from any other part of the body. So for that reason, you shouldn't feel embarrassed or think of yourself as less than anyone else for having these symptoms. Simple ignorance fuels these stereotypes. Everyone usually has more than one person in their family struggling with emotional problems or on medication for stress, depression, or anxiety. You are not in the minority and shouldn't worry about other people's ignorant perspectives. Just continue working with the doctor and other treatment specialists in order to feel better. We love you as we always have and we’ll continue to be there to support you through this difficult time. Please sit down and talk to us about this important issue. Thanks for listening.

I'm very worried that you feel the need to be perfect. I am not sure if we put any pressure on you to feel that you had to be perfect, or it came from somewhere else, but I am concerned that somehow you have the notion that you will be a failure if your performance or achievement is anything less than perfect. First, you really need to understand that there's no such thing as achieving perfection. We are all human beings and there's not a person on the planet that can claim being perfect. We by our own humanity will always be making mistakes. In fact, it is mainly through our mistakes that we learn important lessons in life. If you do make mistakes, the goal should be not to get down on yourself or feel defeated; rather you should identify what the problem is, see if it's fixable and try not to repeat it in the future. You will never be perfect, so striving for it will only leave you depressed and unfulfilled. Instead, try to realize your inner strengths (like the fact that you are kind, loving, honest, etc.) and feel good about who you really are instead of whom you think you should be. Somehow, you need to get over trying to be perfect. It is such an impossible expectation to be placing on yourself and it devours your self-esteem. Know that we think you are great just as you are and so does everyone that knows you. Please don’t be so tough on yourself and accept life's lessons as natural and necessary. You will only face feelings of disappointment and depression if you continue believing that you need to be perfect. By continuing to think of yourself as a perpetual failure you'll never be able to feel good about all the things that should be celebrated in your life. We love you so much and want you to stay on the right track. You are everything a parent would ever want in a child. I just hope someday you will realize that and stop being so hard on yourself. letters.content: We know how painful it is to be betrayed by a friend that you never expected to betray you. A difficult and important part of life is figuring out who are “real friends” and which people are just there for some personal gain. Some people that we call “friends” never intend to give back equally to the relationship.  A real friend is there for you no matter when, where or why you need them. They tend to listen more than give advice and never would judge you, make you feel bad, or hurt you in any way. Some friends that we think of as close friends prove to be just that. However, some will end up betraying us or upsetting us. That is when you’ll need to learn to set limits with them to protect yourself from further hurt. Many so-called real friends will come in and go out of your life. If you realize this fact, the loss will not feel as bad as it feels now. Losing a friend can help you be better at picking new friends that will have values more similar to yours. If you were gossiped about, would you want to befriend a gossiper? If you were put down and humiliated by a friend would you want hang out with people that thought they were better than others? Sometimes we tolerate the mistakes of our friends just to keep the relationship going. However, when the mistakes seem purposeful and repeat themselves over and over, it's probably a red flag to set some limits with that person or possibly eliminate the so-called friendship. We should try to be tolerant when we are being a friend to someone but not at the expense of our own values. If you believe drug dealers were dangerous to our society and provided a negative role model to our youth, would you remain friends with a person that still chose to sell drugs? Sometimes we need to make choices about ending friendships that will be difficult. Not making these decisions can end up hurting us in big ways later. So look out for those friends that might be more takers than givers and try to recognize which friends are truly genuine friends. It'll save a lot of pain and anguish the sooner you learn how to choose better friends. We love you and hope any hurt that comes from friends in your life will be minimal; However, if it does happen, just know that we will always be there for you and are willing to help you through it if you let us. We’ll love you forever and always be here for you.
