I wanted to let you know how much I appreciate the effort you made to not criticize or judge me anymore whenever I try to tell you about a problem I’m having. Even though we’ve gone through some difficult times, I know that you’ve tried very hard to improve this situation. I want you to know that it means a lot to me when I see you caring to make things better. I believe that we should always protect each other from hurt and insist on being respectful towards one another.  Thank you so much for the effort you’re putting into resolving this issue.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility for all the times you've criticized me and made me uncomfortable bringing my problems to you. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we remain supportive of one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I forgive you and hope we can put this behind us.

I know that you think you can’t come to me with your problems because I will criticize you or judge you; but that's not true.  I’m willing to apologize for any hurt that I have caused; but I promise you that I will never do that to you. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us get closer. If you’d like to talk about this, please let me know.

I promise I’ll never judge you if you come to me with your problems. I know that there may be times when you don’t feel comfortable telling me the truth about the problems that you're having.  You really need to feel confident that I am always there for you and would be willing to help you through any difficulty that you may encounter.  I know that at times you worry about my reactions and fear a consequence for telling me that you have made a mistake.  I promise you that if you are open and honest about the troubles you are having, I will never use that information in any way to hurt you or make you regret that you trusted me.  The next time you feel upset or afraid to share your problems, please take a risk and talk to me.  I love you and want to be able to be there to support you throughout your life.

a.) Level l: I don’t trust you enough to come to you when I am having a problem.

I don’t feel I can trust you if I’m having a problem. You are always judging me when I just need you to listen or be supportive. Because of your reactions I avoid talking to you. I am very concerned about our relationship. I shouldn’t have to fear that if I come to you for help, you’ll use that information against me and hurt my feelings. I hope you can start to realize just how much this is hurting our relationship. Please sit down with me so we can talk this out. I’ll be looking forward to our talk. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II: I don’t trust you enough to come to you when I am having a problem.

I have already told you how hurt and upset I am that I don't feel safe coming to you when I'm having a problem. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to make future decisions alone to ensure my own emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and begin to deal with this issue. We need to sit down and talk soon. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III: I don’t trust you enough to come to you when I am having a problem.

I have repeatedly shared with you how upset and hurt I am that I don’t feel I can trust coming to you when I have a problem. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you change your mind and decide you want to work on this, please let me know real soon.  Thanks for listening.

topics.name: It’s important that you know how proud I am of you.

letters.content: I want you to know how sorry I am for not following the rules. The last thing I want to do is make my life more difficult or upset anyone. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner and I promise I will continue to work on this. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into respecting the rules of our house. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to deal with this situation. We all need to improve our lives by managing the problems that affect us most. Every improvement we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the love and concern we have for one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really proud of all the changes you made.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. I wanted to tell you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I realize that I have been disrespecting the rules of the house and need to start obeying them. I really feel bad about the way I have handled myself lately and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I want to tell you how much I appreciate the effort you've made to respect the rules of our house. Even though we’ve gone through some difficult times, I know that you’ve tried really hard to improve this situation. I want you to know that it means a lot to me when I see you caring to make things better. We need to continue to be open with each other and insist on being respectful towards one another. Thank you so much for the effort you’re putting into resolving this issue.

It means a lot to me that you are willing to take responsibility and apologize for not following the rules. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I accept you acknowledging your mistake and forgive you for what happened.

I know that you think I'm not following the rules as closely as I should; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. It’s really unfortunate that this has come between us.  I hope you’re willing to sit down and continue to try to work this out.

I'm very upset that you're not willing to follow the rules of our house. The only way a family works is if we all cooperate with each other so that we can find time to have some happiness in this life. You have been causing a lot of trouble lately by being defiant and stubborn. I'm not sure why you feel that you don't have to follow the rules when everyone else in the household is trying to do their best. I hope you understand that we need everyone to pitch in and do their fair share. I also need you to understand that when I give you a rule to follow I wouldn't be giving it to you if it wasn't important to the entire family in some way. Please try to work with us and not against us and follow the rules that we give to you. It will really make everyone a lot less stressed and feel better about being together as a family. I hope you'll sit down with me to talk about my feelings. Thanks for listening and remember that I’ll always love you.

b.) Level II: - I'm upset that you're not willing to follow the rules.

I told you how concerned I am that you're not willing to follow the rules. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to set even stricter limits in your life to make you understand how important this is. I hope you change your mind and sit down with me soon so we can talk about this. I love you and only want the best for you. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III: - I'm upset that you're not willing to follow the rules.

I have repeatedly shared with you how concerned I am that you’re not willing to follow the rules. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. You’ve left me no other choice but to begin to set even stricter limits in your life until you show me that you recognize how important this is. If you don't want to lose any privileges and decide that you want to work this out, you need to let me know real soon. I hope you decide to talk and I can help you with this. Thanks for listening.

topics.name: It’s important to become more financially independent.

letters.content: I want to thank you for talking to me about the reasons you didn’t tell me I was adopted till I was older. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to talk to me about this situation. Every positive change we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the trust that we share with one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really happy you tried helped me to understand your view on this.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. It’s hard to admit this, but I realize that I waited far too long to tell you that you were adopted. I feel bad that I haven’t been more upfront about this before now. I’d like to sit down and talk to you about this. I really hope you are willing to forgive me so we can put this behind us. Hope to talk to you soon. Thanks for listening.

I wanted to let you know how much I appreciate your effort to talk to me about why you waited so long to tell me I was adopted. I know that you have tried really hard to understand my feelings and made real changes to improve our relationship. I want you to know that it means a lot to me when I see you caring to make things better. I appreciate the effort you’ve put into improving our relationship and your commitment to have open communication in the future is really important to me. We need to continue to be open with each other and insist on being respectful towards one another.    Thank you so much for trying to understand my feelings and making the necessary changes to help our relationship.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility for waiting so long to tell me that I was adopted. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. I know that you’re really trying to be understanding and supportive now. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another.  I forgive you. Thank you so much for caring enough to talk to me about this.

I know that you think I was wrong to wait to tell you that you were adopted, but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. I don’t believe that anyone knows for sure when the best time to tell someone is. Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I know you feel differently about this and it’s really unfortunate that this has come between us. I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve our differences. I wanted you to know how I really felt about this issue. I wish there was something either of us could say or do that would help us work through this problem. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

a.)Level I - Taking responsibility and apologizing for waiting so long to tell you that you were adopted.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for waiting so long to tell you that you were adopted. The last thing I ever wanted to do was to hurt you or make anyone upset. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner and I want to sit down and talk to you about why this happened. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to discuss this with you. I hope you can accept my apology.

I have repeatedly shared with you how upset and hurt I am that you waited so long to tell me that I was adopted. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this.  I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you decide to change your mind and want to talk, please let me know soon.

I have already told you how hurt and upset I am that you failed to tell me I was adopted when I was younger. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to make future decisions that will ensure my own emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and I hear from you soon. Thanks for listening.

I am really upset that you waited this long to tell me that I was adopted. Just because you were afraid I wouldn’t love you as much, you put off a discussion that should have happened when I was much younger. Now I have to deal with a whole new reality at a time when I didn't expect such added stress. I need to know why you waited so long when most professionals believe you should tell a child when they are young. I can forgive you for your error in judgment; however, we need to have a discussion about this. I love you and I hope you can understand how upsetting this is to me. Thanks for listening.

topics.name: It’s important that my daughter is careful when dating boys.

letters.content: I know that you think I regret adopting you, but I have never felt any regret for having adopted you. Even though I feel I haven’t done anything for you to be upset with me, I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you. I know you feel differently about this and it’s really unfortunate that this has come between us. I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve our differences. I wanted you to know how I really felt about this issue. I have never felt that it was a mistake to adopt you. I love you unconditionally and I will never walk out on our relationship. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

For a long time now I have been worried that you think you made a mistake when you adopted me. Whenever we have disagreements or I cause you any pain, I think a lot about how easy your life would be if you never brought me into your family. It really hurts me a lot to think that you may also think that. I know I'm not your biological child but you are all I have. I'm scared that someday I may do something that makes you decide that you don't want me anymore. I worry that you don't love me as much as I love you. I have been afraid to tell you about my insecurities but I needed to tell someone. If you have anything you could say that would help me be less fearful of losing you, I would certainly appreciate you letting me know. I appreciate you listening to me and I hope we can talk about this soon.

a.)Level I - Taking responsibility and apologizing for making you think I regret adopting you.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for making you think I ever regretted adopting you. Even though I have never regretted adopting you, the last thing I ever wanted was to hurt you or make you upset. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this issue sooner and I give my word I’ll do everything I can to make sure you never feel this again. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to share my feelings with you. I hope you can accept my apology.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility for making me feel that you regretted adopting me.  I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. I know that you’re really trying to be understanding and supportive now. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another.  I forgive you. Thank you so much for caring enough to work this out with me.

I wanted to let you know how much I appreciate the effort you made to prove to me that you don't regret adopting me. You and I have made it through a lot of difficult times and we’ve learned to support each other even when our relationship is struggling.  I appreciate the effort you’ve put into improving our relationship. I know if we continue to support one another our relationship will remain strong. Thank you so much for trying to understand my feelings and for being so supportive.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. It’s hard to admit this, but I realize that I have made you feel at times that I regretted adopting you. I feel that I haven’t been honest with myself about this, but I finally need to openly apologize for such hurtful behavior. I’d like to sit down and talk to you about this. I really hope that when you sit down with me you will try to understand and be supportive. I hope we can talk soon. Thanks for listening.

I want to thank you for making me feel that you don’t regret adopting me. I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to help me feel loved unconditionally. Every positive change we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the trust that we share with one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really happy having you as my adoptive parents.

topics.name: It’s important we explain how our marital separation may affect you.

letters.content: I know that you think I'm not preparing myself as quickly as I should for financial independence; but I don’t agree with what you’re saying. If I agreed with you I would certainly take full responsibility. I’m willing to apologize for any mistakes I have made; but I don’t believe I am behind in any goals for becoming financially independent of you. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. It’s really unfortunate that this has come between us.  I hope you’re willing to sit down and continue to try to work this out.

I want you to know how sorry I am for not planning more responsibly how to begin to be more financially independent. The last thing I want to do is make my life more difficult or upset anyone. I want to take full responsibility for not dealing with this problem sooner. I promise to do whatever it takes to learn from this and do the right things in my life that will help me achieve the goal of financial independence. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I am concerned that you're not taking the right steps to become more financially independent at your age. We have tried to teach you the basics of good money management and the importance of hard work and responsibility; but it seems that you're not interested in putting forth the effort to plan out your financial future. In order for you to reach the goal of independence you need to make good decisions regarding school, drugs and alcohol, working hard in a job, choosing good friends and planning on how to become financially independent from us. In order to help you with this, I need to have you start paying your own bills for gas, food, rent, clothes and other personal life expenses. This doesn't mean that I won't ever buy you anything; it just means that I would be putting the majority of responsibility back onto you to become independent. I had to do the same thing when I was your age and I know that you will be able to do this with my help. I love you and will always be there for you whenever you need me. I just think it's important you start to put real effort into becoming truly independent and responsible. Please let's sit down and talk about a plan that we both can agree on. Thanks for listening.

b.) Level II: - I'm concerned that you're not moving towards financial independence as quickly as you should be.

I told you how concerned I am that you're not moving towards financial independence as quickly as you should be. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to set even stricter limits in your life to make you understand how important this is. I hope you change your mind and sit down with me soon so we can talk about this. I love you and only want the best for you. Thanks for listening.

c.) Level III: - I'm concerned that you're not moving towards financial independence as quickly as you should be.

I have repeatedly shared with you how concerned I am that you're not moving towards financial independence as quickly as you should be. I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. You’ve left me no other choice but to begin to set even stricter limits in your life until you show me that you recognize how important this is. If you don't want to lose any privileges and decide that you want to work this out, you need to let me know real soon. I hope you decide to talk and I can help you with this. Thanks for listening.

It means a lot to me that you are willing to take responsibility and apologize for not establishing a better plan to move towards financial independence. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I accept you acknowledging your mistake and forgive you for what happened.

I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into to establishing and following a plan to become financially independent of me. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to deal with this situation. We all need to improve our lives by managing the problems that affect us most. Every improvement we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the love and concern we have for one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really proud of all the changes you made.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. I wanted to tell you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I realize that I haven’t put effort into developing a plan to become financially independent of you and I recognize I need to do this soon. I really feel bad about not preparing myself for independence and I hope you’re willing to talk to me about this. Thanks so much for listening.

I want you to know how proud I am that you have begun to develop a real plan to move towards financial independence. I know it has taken a lot of effort on your part to make better choices and manage this problem. I'm confident that you'll continue to do well if you just remain focused and take one day at a time. You have plenty of people supporting you and I hope you know that I will always be there for you. Try to stay strong and continue to make the right choices in life. You should be proud of all the hard work you’ve put into managing this problem and the respect you've earned as a result.

topics.name: It’s important that you know that I am always here for you to talk to me.

letters.content: I want to thank you for the effort you’ve put into trying to accept my need to adopt a child. I know that it’s not always easy to make certain changes, but I am proud of the commitment you’ve made to deal with this situation. Every positive change we make helps us live to our fullest potential and reinforces the trust that we share with one another. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better. I’m really proud of all the changes you made.

I need to share something with you that I haven’t been able to talk about. It’s hard to admit this, but I realize that I have been wrong to try and leverage you into adopting a child with me. I feel that I haven’t been honest with myself or you about this and it has been a very difficult time in our life. I wanted to get a hold of you sooner but I have been avoiding the issue. I’d like to sit down and talk to you about this. I really hope that when you sit down with me you will try to understand and be supportive. Hope to talk to you soon. Thanks for listening.

I am writing to tell you that I support your decision to adopt a child even if it means ending our relationship. I know how important this is to you. You and I have made it through a lot of difficult times and we’ve learned to support each other even when our relationship was struggling. I know that it is very difficult to deal with these issues. Your decision to adopt child even without me, shows me that you won’t be happy until you follow your dream to have a child. I'm confident that the only way either one of us can find happiness is to support each other even when it's difficult.  I hope you're able to understand my feelings and know that I am behind you even though it may mean losing you.

It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility for trying to leverage me into agreeing to adopt a child. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. I know that you’re really trying to be understanding and supportive now. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another.  I forgive you. Thank you so much for caring enough to work this out with me.

I know you think that I am planning to adopt a child even if you aren’t in agreement, but that's not true. I don’t believe that I would sacrifice our relationship just because you are against adoption. I want to apologize for any hurt that I may have caused you by things I have said in the past. I know you feel differently about this and it’s really unfortunate that this has come between us. I’m willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve our differences. I hope we can talk about this soon. Thanks for listening.

a.)Level I - Taking responsibility and apologizing for deciding to adopt a child without you agreeing to do so.

It really upsets me that I end up hurting the people that mean the most to me. I want to take full responsibility and apologize for telling you that I decided to adopt a child without you agreeing to it. It was wrong of me to leverage you in that way. The last thing I ever wanted to do was to hurt you or make anyone upset. There is no excuse for my behavior. I wanted to let you know that I have made a real commitment to change and that I’m extremely sorry for the problem I have caused. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to consider your feelings. I hope you can accept my apology.

I have repeatedly shared with you that I intend to adopt a child regardless of whether you support me or not .I really don’t understand why you haven’t tried to talk to me about this situation or put any effort into resolving this.  I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but obviously you’ve decided that you’d rather not talk about it. It’s clear that you don’t care about my feelings and that I need to ensure my own emotional health and well-being from this point on. If you decide to change your mind and want to talk, please let me know soon.

I have already told you that I intend to adopt a child regardless of whether you support me or not. I’m disappointed and don’t understand why you haven’t made any attempt to talk to me about this. You should really think about the impact this is having. I hope you’ll make a decision to talk to me soon. If you continue to avoid the issue, I’ll have no choice but to make future decisions that will ensure my own emotional health and well-being. I hope you change your mind and I hear from you soon. Thanks for listening.

I know we've talked about adopting many times and it's clear to me that you're really opposed to it. I really need you to understand that my desire to have a child is so important to me that I am willing to adopt even though you’re unable to support such a decision. I know that if you were to just go along with my decision you would be angry and resentful for having to do something that you are clearly against. Our relationship may not survive such brutal honesty but I need you to know that I am prepared to take on this significant obligation and responsibility by myself if I need to. If adopting a child is the last thing you want to do, then sad as it may be, we will likely have to separate. I wish I could just give up the notion of being a mother but that is impossible for me. I also realize that you shouldn't say yes or agree to something that you are so firmly against. I hope you can understand my feelings on this. Please let’s sit down and talk about this as soon as possible. Thanks for hearing me out.

topics.name: I feel you are getting really selfish and only think about your needs.

letters.content: It means a lot to me that you were willing to take responsibility and sit down with me to try to reconcile our relationship. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I forgive you and hope we can put this behind us.

I know that you think I'm opposed to reconciling with you and improve our relationship; but that’s not true. I would certainly take full responsibility if I thought you were right. Even though I don’t agree with what you’re saying, I would still like to apologize for any hurt that I ever caused you. I agree that we should try to work on reconciling given how short life is. I know we have different feelings about this and I wish we could somehow put this behind us. I'm more than willing to sit down and talk to you if you think it would help us resolve this. If you’d like to talk about this, please let me know.

a.)Level I - Taking responsibility and apologizing for not trying to reconcile the differences in our relationship.

It really bothers me that I hurt the people that I care about the most. I want to apologize and take full responsibility for not trying to reconcile the differences in our relationship sooner. The last thing I ever wanted to do was hurt anyone especially you. I wish I understood why I was acting this way, but there isn’t a good reason. I just wanted to let you know that I'm determined to make a real commitment to change and that I'm extremely sorry for letting this go so long. Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that we needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I have repeatedly shared with you how upset and hurt I am that our relationship has been so disconnected. It’s obvious, that you don’t want to change the way things are. You haven’t shown any effort at all to improve or discuss the situation. I have been patiently waiting to hear from you, but it doesn’t look like that is going to happen. I don’t have any other options but to make decisions that will ensure my own emotional health and well-being. I hope you understand this was not my intent; but without you wanting to work on this, I have no other choice. If you decide that you want to talk about this, you’ll need to let me know real soon. Thanks.

letters.content: Thank you for working with me on a recent parenting challenge. I really felt like we were a team, and it made such a difference. Our ability to listen to each other and compromise in that moment reminded me that we can do this — together

Parenting is a deeply emotional area for me, partly because of how I was raised and the pressure I feel to “get it right.” So when we disagree, it can feel like more than just a difference of opinion — it can feel like a personal attack. I’m sharing this because I want us to understand each other, not fight each other.

I truly believe we can find common ground in how we parent, even if we don’t always agree on the details. I’ve seen us make strong decisions together before — and I know we’re capable of creating a respectful and united front. Let’s keep working on being partners, not opponents.

There were times when I felt unsupported or criticized in my parenting choices, and that left a real emotional mark. But I know you care about the kids just as much as I do — and I want to let go of that resentment so we can co-parent in a healthier way. I forgive you and hope we can move forward with more unity.

I don’t think I’ve been disrespectful — I just have strong opinions about parenting because I want what’s best. But I hear that it may have felt like I was shutting you down, and that’s not what I want. I’m willing to talk about this more and find ways to meet in the middle.

I realize I may have been rigid or dismissive about your parenting style at times, and I’m sorry for that. You have your own reasons and experiences that shape the way you parent, and I want to be more mindful of that. I care about raising our kids together, not tearing each other down in the process.

Since I haven’t seen any effort to acknowledge or address our parenting conflicts, I need to take a step back emotionally. I can’t keep co-parenting in a dynamic that feels divided and dismissive. I need to protect my peace and create boundaries where my parenting voice is respected.

I tried to talk about how our parenting differences have been creating conflict, and I haven’t heard anything back. That silence makes it feel like we’re not really working as a team — and that’s exactly what I was hoping to change. I still want to address this, but I need to know you’re willing to engage.

Even though we don’t always agree on parenting philosophies, we absolutely need to respect each other’s views and choices — not turn it into a source of tension or division. I know we both care deeply about our children and want what’s best for them, even if we have different approaches. But when those differences turn into conflict, judgment, or undermining, it doesn’t just affect us — it affects the kids too. They need consistency, teamwork, and a sense of emotional safety from both of us. I want to be able to discuss parenting decisions with openness and trust, not dread or defensiveness. We won’t always see eye to eye, but we can still work as partners. Can we start focusing on shared goals instead of competing over different methods?

The main thing you must believe is that these symptoms are not any different than having a sore throat from strep, vomiting because of a stomach bug or having fatigue from a heart condition. Instead of being symptoms of your throat, stomach or heart they are symptoms of a different part of your body - your brain. Years ago, we knew very little about the brain. People thought that symptoms such as depression, anxiety, panic attacks, delusions or even hallucinations, were from demons or from some evil source outside the body. How ridiculous that turned out to be. Because science couldn't pinpoint, the source of the symptoms, society made up false reasons for the conditions of the brain. Now we know differently and understand that these symptoms occur just as any other disease does. We now accept that the symptoms originate directly from the neurology and chemistry of the brain. Unfortunately, some of the old thoughts haven’t left society. Some people are still afraid when they see people who have these symptoms. Other people can be cruel and call people names like crazy or insane. Why don’t they make up names for diabetes like sugar wimp or for heart disease like blood pump pansy? Because it makes no sense, that's why. And it's ridiculous that some people are freaked out when they find out their friend or family member has a mental or emotional illness. Society is getting somewhat better and hopefully in the coming decades the public will have enough information for everyone to better understand these issues of the brain more thoroughly. One of the toughest things to do in life is to admit to yourself that you’ve made a mistake. An even tougher test of inner strength is admitting those mistakes to others. Taking responsibility is a problem that we all seem to have growing up. When we were young, we were afraid of consequences. When we were teens we were not only afraid of consequences but we worried about our image. We thought, “What will people think of me if they find out I stole or lied or use drugs or alcohol?” Unfortunately, many people go into adulthood covering up who they really are or trying to cover up the negative patterns they created during their younger years. Some people believe they have to actually deceive others in order to survive. What kind of life would it be, to live a lie and not be honest about whom you are? You are now at a crossroads where choosing to do the right thing may save you from yourself in the long run. You don’t only hurt yourself when you refuse to take responsibility; you hurt a lot of other people as well. The older you get the harder it will be to make this change. One thing is for sure, life changes drastically for the better once you stop lying and admit your mistakes - no matter how big or small. We know that you have had a real hard time with lying and taking responsibility for a long time. You probably even convinced yourself that you were telling the truth in order to be able to live with yourself. It is so important you don’t go into adulthood believing that it's okay to disregard the truth. You will never be able to be real with yourself or anyone until you can stand up and admit your mistakes, take responsibility and stop trying to protect your image with lies. You will never experience true freedom in life without going through this transition. You will just be living a lie. It will be regrettable to live your whole life never having been honest with the people that mattered most to you. You have the opportunity to change all of that now and make a new commitment to yourself. And we will help you in any way you see fit. We love you and want the best for you. Please sit down and talk to us about this serious problem. We need your cooperation to help you through this. Thanks for listening.

letters.content: Thank you for having those difficult conversations with me without shutting down or getting angry. It shows me that we can disagree and still respect each other. That gives me real hope for us.

When we disagree on moral issues, I sometimes question whether we’re truly compatible, and that scares me. I’ve kept that to myself because I didn’t want to start a fight, but I think it’s better if we talk about it openly.

We’re two people with strong minds and hearts — and that can be a strength if we use it well. I believe we can learn from each other’s moral views, not just clash over them. Let’s stay open, even in disagreement.

I forgive you for how our moral conversations have gone in the past. I know we both feel strongly, and I also know we care about each other. I’m willing to keep trying, as long as we both stay committed to respect.

I don’t mean to dismiss your values — I just get really passionate about mine. Sometimes I speak strongly without realizing how it comes across. It’s not that I don’t care about your perspective, I just need to find a better way to express myself.

I’m sorry if I’ve made you feel disrespected or judged during our moral disagreements. I let my emotions get in the way instead of listening with openness. I want you to know that your values matter to me, and I’ll work on being more understanding and fairer.

I understand that people can have different values, but it’s tough when those differences make me feel emotionally distant from you. I want to respect your viewpoint and still feel respected in return, even when we disagree. Lately, I’ve felt like our conversations about right and wrong end up in judgment, frustration, or silence. That’s not what I want for us. I want us to be able to talk about hard topics without shutting down or hurting each other. Can we find a way to listen with curiosity instead of defensiveness — and keep our connection strong, even when our morals diverge?

Can we find a way to do that — to respect each other’s beliefs without feeling threatened or rejected?

topics.name: I Feel Like You’re Not Respecting My Physical or Sexual Boundaries

letters.content: Thank you for listening and taking my boundaries seriously. I’ve noticed your effort to respect what I need, and it’s made me feel safer and more valued. That kind of growth matters deeply to me.

It’s really hard for me to talk about this, but I need to be honest — when you ignore my boundaries, it feels violating. It makes me want to shut down emotionally and physically. I need you to truly understand how deep this goes.

Respecting physical and sexual boundaries is one of the most important parts of a relationship. I believe you can show me the care, patience, and maturity needed to make this relationship feel safe for both of us.

I forgive you for not respecting my physical and sexual boundaries. That doesn’t mean it didn’t hurt or that it was okay — but I believe that if you’re truly willing to change, we can work toward rebuilding trust.

I didn’t mean to make you feel unsafe or disrespected. I thought I was being playful, but I now realize that it wasn’t okay and that I crossed a line. I want to learn how to better respect your comfort and boundaries moving forward.

I’m truly sorry for crossing your physical and sexual boundaries. I now realize that my behavior hurt you and made you feel unsafe. That was wrong. I should have taken you seriously the first time, and I will work on earning back your trust through real change.

Since I haven’t seen a change or heard a response, I need to prioritize my emotional and physical safety. I can’t be in a relationship where my boundaries are ignored or minimized. Until I feel that you respect me in this way, I need distance.

I brought up my feelings about how you’ve handled my physical and sexual boundaries, but I haven’t heard anything from you. That silence worries me even more. I need to know that you’re thinking about this and willing to take it seriously.

I’ve talked to you before about respecting physical and sexual boundaries in our relationship, but based on what happened recently, it feels like you either don’t care or treat it like a joke — and that really hurts me and affects my trust. Boundaries are not about rejection or control; they are about safety, comfort, and respect. When I tell you what I need or what makes me uncomfortable, I need to know that you take it seriously. When those boundaries are crossed, it’s not just uncomfortable — it makes me feel unsafe and disregarded. I shouldn’t have to keep repeating myself about something so personal. This is not a small issue. Please take some time to reflect on how serious this is and what it means for us.

topics.name: I Feel You’re Not Respecting the Interracial Differences Affecting Our Relationship

letters.content: Thank you for being open to hearing how our racial differences impact me. It means a lot when you listen, ask questions, and show that you care. It gives me hope for how we’ll continue to grow as a couple.

Sometimes I wonder if you really understand how our interracial dynamic shapes the way I experience the world — and our relationship. I’ve held that in because I didn’t want to create distance between us, but I think we need to start having more open and honest conversations about it.

This relationship is important to me, and I believe we can grow stronger by facing the tough topics together. I don’t expect perfection — just a willingness to learn and be there for each other, especially when cultural differences come up.

I forgive you for the times you didn’t fully acknowledge how our racial and cultural backgrounds affect us. I know it’s hard to talk about, but I believe we can move forward together with more understanding and empathy.

I never meant to ignore or minimize the differences in our backgrounds. I guess I didn’t realize how much it was affecting you or our relationship. I’m not trying to avoid the topic — I just don’t always know how to talk about it.

I’m sorry if I’ve been insensitive or failed to see how our racial differences have impacted you. I’ve been afraid or unsure how to respond, but I realize now that silence only creates more distance. I want to learn, grow, and do better for us.
Since you haven’t responded, I’m going to step back and focus on my emotional needs for now. This is an important issue to me, and I’m still open to reconnecting when you feel ready to engage.

I brought up how our racial and cultural differences affect me in this relationship, but I haven’t heard back from you. I still want to understand your perspective too — and I’m hoping we can talk about it together.

Being in an interracial relationship brings both love and challenges, and lately I’ve felt like some of those challenges aren’t being fully acknowledged between us. I know we didn’t choose each other for our backgrounds, but those backgrounds still shape how the world sees us — and how we sometimes see each other. There are moments when I feel like you don’t quite understand the weight I carry from societal expectations or experiences with bias. I don’t expect you to have all the answers, but I do need to feel like you’re willing to try to understand and support me when it gets hard. Avoiding the topic or minimizing the impact it has on our relationship only pushes us further apart. I care deeply about you and want to strengthen our connection. Can we start talking about what this means for both of us — and how we can better support each other through it?

topics.name: I Feel Power Struggles with My Colleagues/Coworkers

letters.content: It’s not easy to move past the way I’ve felt treated, but I’m open to forgiving the tension and trying again — if we can approach things with more collaboration going forward.

I’ve held back some thoughts for fear of making things worse, but it’s been affecting me more than I let on. The constant push-and-pull dynamic is draining and discouraging.
I believe we’re both capable of working through this. If we can focus on communication instead of control, I really think we could have a productive and respectful working relationship.
I wasn’t trying to exert control or cause tension — I just have a strong sense of how things should go. But I hear your concerns and want to try and understand your perspective better.
I’m sorry if I’ve made you feel dismissed or disrespected. I realize now that my approach may have come across as controlling, and I want to work on fostering mutual respect.
I’ve tried to express my concerns respectfully, but I can’t keep subjecting myself to an unhealthy power dynamic. I’m choosing to protect my own emotional well-being now.
I brought up my concerns because I care about this environment and my role in it. I’m still hoping we can address the unhealthy dynamic of power struggles and move toward mutual respect.

It often feels like there’s a constant power struggle between us, and rather than fostering collaboration or respect, it creates tension and frustration. I want to be able to contribute, communicate, and work effectively, but it seems like there’s a need to assert control rather than seek solutions. When I try to offer input or raise concerns, I feel dismissed or undermined. That dynamic makes it hard to stay motivated or engaged, and I’m concerned that it’s hurting the overall team environment. I’m not asking for special treatment — I’m asking for mutual respect and recognition of what each of us brings. I want to find a healthier way to interact without constant conflict or defensiveness. Can we work toward a more respectful and cooperative approach?

topics.name: I Feel Like You’re Not Respecting My Digital and Social Media Privacy

letters.content: I feel like you’re not respecting my privacy when you go through my phone, messages, or social media without asking. Even if you’re doing it out of curiosity or concern, it still crosses a personal boundary. Everyone deserves digital space and trust in a relationship. When you go through my things without my knowledge or permission, it makes me feel violated and distrusted. Privacy doesn’t mean hiding something — it means having the right to a little autonomy. I need you to understand that constantly checking my digital life breaks down the trust we’re supposed to be building. Please respect that boundary if we want to move forward in a healthy way.

I spoke to you about how hurtful it feels when you don’t respect my digital boundaries, but I haven’t gotten any kind of response. That silence makes it harder for me to believe that this will change. I need to know that you’re hearing me.

Since you haven’t responded or changed your behavior, I need to create stronger boundaries myself. My digital life is part of my personal space, and until I feel it’s respected, I’ll be limiting what I share and how available I am.

I’m sorry for going through your phone or social media without your permission. I now realize how deeply that crossed a boundary and made you feel unsafe and disrespected. I promise to honor your privacy from now on and rebuild the trust I damaged.

I didn’t mean to invade your privacy — I acted out of insecurity, not malice. Still, I see how that made you feel untrusted and exposed. I want to earn your trust without needing to look through your private life again.

I forgive you for crossing that boundary. It hurt, and it took away some of my sense of personal freedom. But I also believe that with better communication, we can create a relationship rooted in mutual respect and trust.

Trusting someone’s digital privacy is just as important as trusting their actions. You don’t need to check my devices to feel safe — real safety comes from honest conversations and respecting boundaries. I believe you can do that.

It’s not easy to say this, but when you check my phone or social media without asking, it makes me feel like I’ve lost a part of myself in this relationship. I want to feel trusted and free — not watched or controlled.
Thank you for respecting my digital space. It’s helped me feel safer and more like an equal in this relationship. Your effort to build trust in this way means a lot to me.

topics.name: I Feel You Are Disrespecting My Time

letters.content: Thank you for making the effort to respect my time and space. Whether it was giving me quiet when I needed it or checking in before making plans, those actions really mattered. It helped me feel seen and respected in a way I had been missing. I truly appreciate the shift.

It feels like you regularly disregard my personal time, energy, or space — and that’s starting to take a real toll on me. There are moments when I need quiet, rest, or uninterrupted time, and it doesn’t feel like that’s respected. I’ve tried to communicate those needs, but I often end up feeling guilty for asking or ignored altogether. When my space or schedule gets pushed aside, it makes me feel like what matters to me doesn’t matter to you. Everyone has limits, and I’m reaching mine. I want to be close to you, but not at the cost of my own capacity and well-being. Can we talk about how to respect each other’s time and space more intentionally?

I opened up about how I’ve been feeling drained and disrespected when it comes to my time and space, but I haven’t heard anything back. That silence feels like a continuation of the same disregard I was trying to talk about. If this relationship is going to work, I need to know that my limits are being heard and considered — not dismissed.

After saying what I needed and still getting no real response or change, I’ve realized I need to step back and protect my time, space, and energy more actively. I can’t keep giving without boundaries — it’s not sustainable. This isn’t about punishing you; it’s about reclaiming my well-being. I hope someday we can revisit this with mutual respect, but for now, I need distance.

I can see now that I’ve sometimes overlooked your need for time or space, and I want to take responsibility for that. It wasn’t my intention to crowd you or disregard your boundaries. I’m sorry for any moments where I pushed too hard or asked too much without recognizing your limits. I want to do better going forward.

I didn’t realize I was being disrespectful of your time or space. I may not have fully understood how much you needed those things in the moment. I was acting from a place of wanting connection, not control. That said, I’m open to learning what your limits are so I can be more respectful of them moving forward.

There were times when I felt like I was being stretched too thin, like my needs weren’t being honored. That left me feeling depleted and unimportant. But I also know we all have blind spots, and I believe yours came from a place of unawareness, not malice. I forgive you, and I hope we can rebuild with better understanding and boundaries.

I believe we can create a dynamic where both of us feel respected and replenished instead of drained. I’ve seen glimpses of that — moments where you’ve paused, listened, and adjusted. That means a lot. Let’s keep building a rhythm that honors both of our needs, not just one side.

I’ve always had a hard time setting boundaries — especially around my time and energy. I often say yes when I mean no, and then end up feeling overwhelmed or taken for granted. So when I finally do speak up and still don’t feel heard, it hits hard. I’m sharing this not to place blame, but to explain why this issue feels so important to me.

topics.name: I Feel You’re Not Respecting Holiday or Religious Ritual Conflicts in Our Relationship

letters.content: Since I haven’t heard from you, I’m going to take care of my emotional space and do what I need during the holidays in a way that honors me. I’m still open to working through it together when you’re ready.

I know that these traditions mean different things to both of us, but that’s exactly why we need to be intentional about how we approach them. When one person’s needs or traditions are overlooked or dismissed, it creates feelings of resentment and disconnection. I don’t want to pressure you into doing something you’re uncomfortable with, but I also don’t want to feel like my own traditions or values are being ignored. We both deserve to feel seen and respected during these important times. Let’s talk openly about what each of us needs — and how we can make space for both of our practices, beliefs, or ways of celebrating.

As much as that may be true, it doesn’t teach them the full lesson that we are trying to get across to them. It also gives them the idea that they can manipulate out of their remaining consequence. I know that you are sincerely sorry and I appreciate all of your effort to make this situation better. We all have to deal with stressful times in life, but it’s important that we stay respectful towards one another during those difficult moments. I hope going forward we’ll protect each other from hurt rather than cause it for one another. I forgive you and hope we can put this behind us.

Even though we’ve gone through some difficult times, you’ve tried really hard to improve this situation. I want you to know that it means a lot to me when I see you caring to make things better. I believe that we should always protect each other from hurt and insist on being respectful towards one another. Thank you so much for the effort you’re putting into resolving this issue.

I look forward to getting together with you.

We all need to improve our lives by strengthening the relationships that mean the most to us. Every improvement we make will help us live to our fullest potential and reinforce the love and concern we have for each other. Thanks so much for all of your effort to make things better.

If you’d like to talk about this, please let me know.

Thank you for caring enough to confront me about this and for helping me to understand that I needed to make some changes. I hope you can accept my apology.

I hope you change your mind and begin to deal with this issue. We need to sit down and talk soon. Thanks for listening.

letters.content: Thank you for working with me on a recent parenting challenge. I really felt like we were a team, and it made such a difference. Our ability to listen to each other and compromise in that moment reminded me that we can do this — together

Parenting is a deeply emotional area for me, partly because of how I was raised and the pressure I feel to “get it right.” So when we disagree, it can feel like more than just a difference of opinion — it can feel like a personal attack. I’m sharing this because I want us to understand each other, not fight each other.

I truly believe we can find common ground in how we parent, even if we don’t always agree on the details. I’ve seen us make strong decisions together before — and I know we’re capable of creating a respectful and united front. Let’s keep working on being partners, not opponents.

There were times when I felt unsupported or criticized in my parenting choices, and that left a real emotional mark. But I know you care about the kids just as much as I do — and I want to let go of that resentment so we can co-parent in a healthier way. I forgive you and hope we can move forward with more unity.

I don’t think I’ve been disrespectful — I just have strong opinions about parenting because I want what’s best. But I hear that it may have felt like I was shutting you down, and that’s not what I want. I’m willing to talk about this more and find ways to meet in the middle.

I realize I may have been rigid or dismissive about your parenting style at times, and I’m sorry for that. You have your own reasons and experiences that shape the way you parent, and I want to be more mindful of that. I care about raising our kids together, not tearing each other down in the process.

Since I haven’t seen any effort to acknowledge or address our parenting conflicts, I need to take a step back emotionally. I can’t keep co-parenting in a dynamic that feels divided and dismissive. I need to protect my peace and create boundaries where my parenting voice is respected.

I tried to talk about how our parenting differences have been creating conflict, and I haven’t heard anything back. That silence makes it feel like we’re not really working as a team — and that’s exactly what I was hoping to change. I still want to address this, but I need to know you’re willing to engage.

Even though we don’t always agree on parenting philosophies, we absolutely need to respect each other’s views and choices — not turn it into a source of tension or division. I know we both care deeply about our children and want what’s best for them, even if we have different approaches. But when those differences turn into conflict, judgment, or undermining, it doesn’t just affect us — it affects the kids too. They need consistency, teamwork, and a sense of emotional safety from both of us. I want to be able to discuss parenting decisions with openness and trust, not dread or defensiveness. We won’t always see eye to eye, but we can still work as partners. Can we start focusing on shared goals instead of competing over different methods?

I’ve spent a lot of my life having to carry my emotions alone, and when that happens again in a relationship, it hits something really raw. I’m telling you this so you know where my need comes from — it’s not about weakness, it’s about history.

I believe you can be emotionally present — I’ve seen you show kindness, empathy, and care in other ways. I think sometimes you just don’t know how much it matters, or how to show it when things get hard. I hope you’ll lean into that more, because emotional support is something we both need and deserve.

There have been moments when I felt emotionally abandoned — like I was going through something hard and you weren’t really there. That hurt me deeply. But I also believe that support isn’t always easy for everyone to know how to give. I forgive you, and I hope we can learn to be more present for each other going forward.

I never meant to make you feel unsupported — in fact, I thought I was being there for you in my own way. Maybe I didn’t express it in the way you needed, and I’m open to learning more about what that looks like for you. I care deeply, even if it hasn’t always come across the way you needed it to.

I see now that I haven’t always been emotionally available for you, and I’m truly sorry. Whether I was distracted, overwhelmed, or just unsure how to show up — I recognize the impact it had. You deserved more presence, more care, and more support than I gave. I want to do better, starting now.

Since I’ve reached out about needing emotional support and still haven’t seen any acknowledgment or effort, I have to step back to care for myself. I can’t keep reaching out and getting nothing in return — it’s draining and lonely. I need space to reconnect with what nurtures me, even if that means creating distance in this relationship for now.

There are times when I feel like I have no emotional support from you, and it’s honestly scary to feel so alone in a relationship that’s supposed to be close. When I’m going through something difficult and you seem distant or disengaged, it leaves me feeling even more vulnerable. I want to feel like I can turn to you when I’m hurting — not like I have to manage everything on my own. Being emotionally available isn’t about having all the answers — it’s about showing up, listening, and caring.
